5.2.5       System Control
            For power-savings purposes, the RCGCn , SCGCn , and DCGCn registers control the clock gating
            logic for each peripheral or block in the system while the controller is in Run, Sleep, and Deep-Sleep
            mode, respectively.
            There are four levels of operation for the device defined as:

            ■ Run Mode. In Run mode, the controller actively executes code. Run mode provides normal
              operation of the processor and all of the peripherals that are currently enabled by the RCGCn
              registers. The system clock can be any of the available clock sources including the PLL.

            ■ Sleep Mode. In Sleep mode, the clock frequency of the active peripherals is unchanged, but the
              processor and the memory subsystem are not clocked and therefore no longer execute code.
              Sleep mode is entered by the Cortex-M3 core executing a WFI(Wait for Interrupt)
              instruction. Any properly configured interrupt event in the system will bring the processor back
              into Run mode. See “Power Management” on page 90 for more details.
                Peripherals are clocked that are enabled in the SCGCn register when auto-clock gating is enabled
                (see the RCC register) or the RCGCn register when the auto-clock gating is disabled. The system
                clock has the same source and frequency as that during Run mode.

            ■ Deep-Sleep Mode. In Deep-Sleep mode, the clock frequency of the active peripherals may
              change (depending on the Run mode clock configuration) in addition to the processor clock being
              stopped. An interrupt returns the device to Run mode from one of the sleep modes; the sleep
              modes are entered on request from the code. Deep-Sleep mode is entered by first writing the
              Deep Sleep Enable bit in the ARM Cortex-M3 NVIC system control register and then executing

July 15, 2014                                                                                                  183
                                      Texas Instruments-Production Data
System Control

                 a WFI instruction. Any properly configured interrupt event in the system will bring the processor
                 back into Run mode. See “Power Management” on page 90 for more details.
                 The Cortex-M3 processor core and the memory subsystem are not clocked. Peripherals are
                 clocked that are enabled in the DCGCn register when auto-clock gating is enabled (see the RCC
                 register) or the RCGCn register when auto-clock gating is disabled. The system clock source is
                 the main oscillator by default or the internal oscillator specified in the DSLPCLKCFG register if
                 one is enabled. When the DSLPCLKCFG register is used, the internal oscillator is powered up,
                 if necessary, and the main oscillator is powered down. If the PLL is running at the time of the
                 WFI instruction, hardware will power the PLL down and override the SYSDIV field of the active
                 RCC/RCC2 register, to be determined by the DSDIVORIDE setting in the DSLPCLKCFG register,
                 up to /16 or /64 respectively. When the Deep-Sleep exit event occurs, hardware brings the system
                 clock back to the source and frequency it had at the onset of Deep-Sleep mode before enabling
                 the clocks that had been stopped during the Deep-Sleep duration.

           ■ Hibernate Mode. In this mode, the power supplies are turned off to the main part of the device
             and only the Hibernation module's circuitry is active. An external wake event or RTC event is
             required to bring the device back to Run mode. The Cortex-M3 processor and peripherals outside
             of the Hibernation module see a normal "power on" sequence and the processor starts running
             code. It can determine that it has been restarted from Hibernate mode by inspecting the
             Hibernation module registers.

           Caution – If the Cortex-M3 Debug Access Port (DAP) has been enabled, and the device wakes from a
           low power sleep or deep-sleep mode, the core may start executing code before all clocks to peripherals
           have been restored to their run mode configuration. The DAP is usually enabled by software tools
           accessing the JTAG or SWD interface when debugging or flash programming. If this condition occurs,
           a Hard Fault is triggered when software accesses a peripheral with an invalid clock.
           A software delay loop can be used at the beginning of the interrupt routine that is used to wake up a
           system from a WFI (Wait For Interrupt) instruction. This stalls the execution of any code that accesses
           a peripheral register that might cause a fault. This loop can be removed for production software as the
           DAP is most likely not enabled during normal execution.
           Because the DAP is disabled by default (power on reset), the user can also power-cycle the device. The
           DAP is not enabled unless it is enabled through the JTAG or SWD interface.

           1. Bypass the PLL and system clock divider by setting the BYPASS bit and clearing the USESYS
              bit in the RCC register. This configures the system to run off a “raw” clock source and allows

/*
 * microSD block service for the EK-LM3S6965 evaluation board.
 *
 * The host drives the card through UART0 (virtual COM port, 115200 8N1).
 * One command per line ('\n'), answered with one line:
 *
 *   I                    initialise the card  -> "OK SDSC", "OK SDHC", "OK SDV1" or "ERR <n>"
 *   R <lba>              read block <lba>     -> "DATA <1024 hex digits>" or "ERR <n>"
 *   W <lba> <1024 hex>   write block <lba>    -> "OK" or "ERR <n>"
 *
 * <lba> is a decimal 512-byte block number. "READY" is printed once after
 * reset. A malformed line is answered with "ERR 0".
 *
 * The system clock is 50 MHz from the 8 MHz crystal through the PLL.
 * The card runs on SSI0 in SPI mode (Freescale mode 0, SPO=0 SPH=0,
 * software chip select on PD0): 400 kHz during identification, 12.5 MHz
 * for data transfers.
 */
#include <stdint.h>

#define REG(a)          (*(volatile uint32_t *)(a))

/* System control */
#define SYSCTL_DID0     REG(0x400FE000)
#define SYSCTL_LDOPCTL  REG(0x400FE034)
#define SYSCTL_RIS      REG(0x400FE050)
#define SYSCTL_RCC      REG(0x400FE060)
#define SYSCTL_RCC2     REG(0x400FE070)
#define SYSCTL_RCGC1    REG(0x400FE104)
#define SYSCTL_RCGC2    REG(0x400FE108)

#define RCGC1_UART0     0x00000001u
#define RCGC1_SSI0      0x00000010u
#define RCGC2_GPIOA     0x00000001u
#define RCGC2_GPIOD     0x00000008u

#define RCC_XTAL_8MHZ   0x00000380u     /* XTAL = 8 MHz (PLLCFG translation) */
#define RCC_OSCSRC      0x00000030u
#define RCC_OSCSRC_MOSC 0x00000000u     /* main oscillator */
#define RCC_MOSCDIS     0x00000001u
#define RCC_PWRDN       0x00002000u
#define RCC_BYPASS      0x00000800u
#define RCC_USESYSDIV   0x00400000u
#define RCC_SYSDIV      0x07800000u
#define RCC_SYSDIV_8    0x03800000u     /* 400 MHz PLL / 8 = 50 MHz */
#define RIS_PLLLRIS     0x00000040u

/* GPIO; the data register is addressed through a bit mask in address bits [9:2] */
#define GPIOA_BASE      0x40004000u
#define GPIOD_BASE      0x40007000u
#define GPIO_DATA(b, m) REG((b) + ((uint32_t)(m) << 2))
#define GPIO_DIR(b)     REG((b) + 0x400u)
#define GPIO_AFSEL(b)   REG((b) + 0x420u)
#define GPIO_DEN(b)     REG((b) + 0x51Cu)

/* UART0 */
#define UART0_DR        REG(0x4000C000)
#define UART0_FR        REG(0x4000C018)
#define UART0_IBRD      REG(0x4000C024)
#define UART0_FBRD      REG(0x4000C028)
#define UART0_LCRH      REG(0x4000C02C)
#define UART0_CTL       REG(0x4000C030)
#define UART_FR_RXFE    0x10u
#define UART_FR_TXFF    0x20u

/* SSI0 */
#define SSI0_CR0        REG(0x40008000)
#define SSI0_CR1        REG(0x40008004)
#define SSI0_DR         REG(0x40008008)
#define SSI0_SR         REG(0x4000800C)
#define SSI0_CPSR       REG(0x40008010)
#define SSI_CR1_SSE     0x02u
#define SSI_SR_TNF      0x02u
#define SSI_SR_RNE      0x04u

#define SD_CS           0x01u           /* PD0, card select, active low */

enum { CARD_NONE = -1, CARD_SDSC, CARD_SDHC, CARD_SDV1 };
static const char *const card_name[] = { "SDSC", "SDHC", "SDV1" };

static int card = CARD_NONE;

/* ---- clock ---------------------------------------------------------------- */

/*
 * 50 MHz system clock: 8 MHz crystal on the main oscillator, PLL at 400 MHz
 * divided by 8 (SYSDIV=3, USESYSDIV=1).  The boards carry Fury-class rev A2
 * silicon, so the LDO must be raised from the 2.50 V default to 2.75 V before
 * the PLL is powered up (erratum LM3SYSCTL#09); running the PLL at the
 * default LDO setting causes unstable behaviour.
 */
#define SYSCLK_HZ       50000000u

static uint32_t clock_init(void)
{
    uint32_t rcc;

    SYSCTL_LDOPCTL = 0x1B;              /* LDO 2.75 V, required before the PLL runs */

    /* Run from the main oscillator with the PLL bypassed while it locks. */
    rcc = SYSCTL_RCC;
    rcc |= RCC_BYPASS | RCC_PWRDN;
    rcc &= ~(RCC_XTAL_8MHZ | (RCC_XTAL_8MHZ * 0 + 0x3C0u) /*replaced below*/);
    (void)rcc;
    SYSCTL_RCC = (SYSCTL_RCC | RCC_BYPASS | RCC_PWRDN) & ~RCC_USESYSDIV;
    SYSCTL_RCC = (SYSCTL_RCC & ~RCC_SYSDIV) | RCC_SYSDIV_8 | RCC_USESYSDIV;
    SYSCTL_RCC = (SYSCTL_RCC & ~(RCC_OSCSRC | RCC_XTAL_MASK)) | RCC_XTAL_8MHZ | RCC_OSCSRC_MOSC;
    SYSCTL_RCC &= ~RCC_MOSCDIS;         /* main oscillator enable */
    SYSCTL_RCC &= ~RCC_PWRDN;           /* power the PLL; it locks onto the XTAL setting */
    while (!(SYSCTL_RIS & RIS_PLLLRIS))
        ;                               /* wait for the PLL TREADY timer */
    SYSCTL_RCC &= ~RCC_BYPASS;          /* switch the system clock to the PLL */

    return SYSCLK_HZ;
}

/* ---- UART0 ---------------------------------------------------------------- */

static void uart_init(uint32_t sysclk)
{
    uint32_t div64;

    SYSCTL_RCGC1 |= RCGC1_UART0;
    SYSCTL_RCGC2 |= RCGC2_GPIOA;
    (void)SYSCTL_RCGC2;                 /* a few clocks before the modules are touched */

    GPIO_AFSEL(GPIOA_BASE) |= 0x03;     /* PA0 U0RX, PA1 U0TX */
    GPIO_DEN(GPIOA_BASE) |= 0x03;

    /* divisor = sysclk / (16 * 115200) in 1/64 steps, rounded */
    div64 = (sysclk * 4u + 57600u) / 115200u;
    UART0_CTL = 0;
    UART0_IBRD = div64 >> 6;
    UART0_FBRD = div64 & 0x3Fu;
    UART0_LCRH = 0x70;                  /* 8 data bits, no parity, 1 stop bit, FIFOs on */
    UART0_CTL = 0x301;                  /* UARTEN, TXE, RXE */
}

static void uart_putc(char c)
{
    while (UART0_FR & UART_FR_TXFF)
        ;
    UART0_DR = (uint8_t)c;
}

static void uart_puts(const char *s)
{
    while (*s)
        uart_putc(*s++);
}

static void uart_putu(uint32_t v)
{
    char buf[11];
    int n = 0;

    do {
        buf[n++] = (char)('0' + v % 10u);
        v /= 10u;
    } while (v);
    while (n)
        uart_putc(buf[--n]);
}

static char uart_getc(void)
{
    while (UART0_FR & UART_FR_RXFE)
        ;
    return (char)(UART0_DR & 0xFFu);
}

/* ---- SSI0 ----------------------------------------------------------------- */

/*
 * SPI mode 0 (SPO = 0, SPH = 0), 8-bit frames, software chip select.
 * PA3/SSI0FSS is deliberately left out of the alternate function: it is the
 * OLED display's chip select on this board, and asserting it on every SSI
 * transfer feeds the card traffic to the display.
 */
static void ssi_init(void)
{
    SYSCTL_RCGC1 |= RCGC1_SSI0;
    SYSCTL_RCGC2 |= RCGC2_GPIOA | RCGC2_GPIOD;
    (void)SYSCTL_RCGC2;

    /* SSI0 on PA2 (clock), PA4 (rx) and PA5 (tx); PA3 stays a GPIO input */
    GPIO_AFSEL(GPIOA_BASE) |= 0x34;
    GPIO_DEN(GPIOA_BASE) |= 0x34;

    /* PD0 drives the card select; idle high */
    GPIO_DIR(GPIOD_BASE) |= SD_CS;
    GPIO_DEN(GPIOD_BASE) |= SD_CS;
    GPIO_DATA(GPIOD_BASE, SD_CS) = SD_CS;

    /* master, Freescale SPI mode 0, 8-bit frames, 400 kHz for card identification */
    SSI0_CR1 = 0;
    SSI0_CPSR = SYSCLK_HZ / 400000u;    /* even divisor, SCR = 0 */
    SSI0_CR0 = 0x0007;
    SSI0_CR1 = SSI_CR1_SSE;
}

/* Raise the bit rate once the card has left the identification phase. */
static void ssi_fast(void)
{
    SSI0_CR1 = 0;
    SSI0_CPSR = 4;                      /* 50 MHz / 4 = 12.5 MHz */
    SSI0_CR1 = SSI_CR1_SSE;
}

/* Back to the identification rate for a (possibly new) card. */
static void ssi_slow(void)
{
    SSI0_CR1 = 0;
    SSI0_CPSR = SYSCLK_HZ / 400000u;
    SSI0_CR1 = SSI_CR1_SSE;
}

static uint8_t spi(uint8_t out)
{
    while (!(SSI0_SR & SSI_SR_TNF))
        ;
    SSI0_DR = out;
    while (!(SSI0_SR & SSI_SR_RNE))
        ;
    return (uint8_t)SSI0_DR;
}

/* ---- SD card in SPI mode -------------------------------------------------- */

static void card_select(void)
{
    GPIO_DATA(GPIOD_BASE, SD_CS) = 0;
    spi(0xFF);
}

static void card_deselect(void)
{
    GPIO_DATA(GPIOD_BASE, SD_CS) = SD_CS;
    spi(0xFF);                          /* lets the card release its data out line */
}

/* Send a command frame and return R1, or 0xFF if the card does not answer. */
static uint8_t sd_command(uint8_t cmd, uint32_t arg, uint8_t crc)
{
    uint8_t r1;
    int n;

    for (n = 0; n < 1000; n++)                          /* >= 8 clocks since the last response, card not busy */
        if (spi(0xFF) == 0xFF)
            break;
    spi((uint8_t)(0x40u | cmd));
    spi((uint8_t)(arg >> 24));
    spi((uint8_t)(arg >> 16));
    spi((uint8_t)(arg >> 8));
    spi((uint8_t)arg);
    spi(crc);
    for (n = 0; n < 10; n++) {
        r1 = spi(0xFF);
        if (!(r1 & 0x80u))
            return r1;
    }
    return 0xFF;
}

static int sd_init(void)
{
    uint8_t r1 = 0xFF, r3[4];
    int n;
    int sdv2 = 0;

    ssi_slow();                                         /* 100-400 kHz while the card is identified */

    /* at least 74 clocks with the card deselected */
    GPIO_DATA(GPIOD_BASE, SD_CS) = SD_CS;
    for (n = 0; n < 12; n++)
        spi(0xFF);

    card_select();
    if (sd_command(0, 0, 0x95) != 0x01) {               /* GO_IDLE_STATE */
        card_deselect();
        return -1;
    }
    r1 = sd_command(8, 0x000001AAu, 0x87);              /* SEND_IF_COND */
    if (r1 == 0x01) {
        uint8_t r7[4];

        for (n = 0; n < 4; n++)
            r7[n] = spi(0xFF);
        if (r7[3] != 0xAA) {                            /* echo did not come back */
            card_deselect();
            return -3;
        }
        sdv2 = 1;
    } else if (r1 != 0x05) {                            /* not idle and not "illegal command" */
        card_deselect();
        return -2;
    }
    if (sdv2) {                                         /* SD 2.00 or later */
        for (n = 0; n < 2000; n++) {
            sd_command(55, 0, 0x01);
            r1 = sd_command(41, 0x40000000u, 0x01);     /* ACMD41 with HCS */
            if (r1 == 0x00)
                break;
        }
        if (r1 != 0x00) {
            card_deselect();
            return -4;
        }
        if (sd_command(58, 0, 0x01) != 0x00) {          /* READ_OCR */
            card_deselect();
            return -6;
        }
        for (n = 0; n < 4; n++)
            r3[n] = spi(0xFF);
        if (r3[0] & 0x40u) {                            /* CCS: block-addressed high capacity card */
            card_deselect();
            ssi_fast();
            return CARD_SDHC;
        }
    } else {                                            /* version 1.x: ACMD41 first, plain CMD1 after that */
        for (n = 0; n < 2000; n++) {
            sd_command(55, 0, 0x01);
            r1 = sd_command(41, 0, 0x01);               /* no HCS on a 1.x card */
            if (r1 == 0x00)
                break;
            if (r1 & 0x04u) {                           /* ACMD41 rejected: try the MMC way */
                r1 = sd_command(1, 0, 0x01);
                if (r1 == 0x00)
                    break;
            }
        }
        if (r1 != 0x00) {
            card_deselect();
            return -4;
        }
    }

    r1 = sd_command(16, 512, 0x01);                     /* SET_BLOCKLEN for byte-addressed cards */
    card_deselect();
    if (r1 != 0x00)
        return -5;

    ssi_fast();
    return sdv2 ? CARD_SDSC : CARD_SDV1;
}

/* Block address for a read or write: byte address for SDSC/SDV1, block index for SDHC. */
static uint32_t sd_addr(uint32_t lba)
{
    return card == CARD_SDHC ? lba : lba * 512u;
}

static int sd_read(uint32_t lba, uint8_t *buf)
{
    uint8_t tok = 0xFF;
    int n;

    card_select();
    if (sd_command(17, sd_addr(lba), 0x01) != 0x00) {   /* READ_SINGLE_BLOCK */
        card_deselect();
        return -1;
    }
    for (n = 0; n < 100000 && tok == 0xFF; n++)
        tok = spi(0xFF);
    if (tok != 0xFE) {
        card_deselect();
        return -2;
    }
    for (n = 0; n < 512; n++)
        buf[n] = spi(0xFF);
    spi(0xFF);                                          /* CRC, not checked */
    spi(0xFF);
    card_deselect();
    return 0;
}

static int sd_write(uint32_t lba, const uint8_t *buf)
{
    uint8_t resp;
    int n;

    card_select();
    if (sd_command(24, sd_addr(lba), 0x01) != 0x00) {   /* WRITE_BLOCK */
        card_deselect();
        return -1;
    }
    spi(0xFF);
    spi(0xFE);                                          /* start block token */
    for (n = 0; n < 512; n++)
        spi(buf[n]);
    spi(0xFF);                                          /* CRC, not checked by the card */
    spi(0xFF);
    resp = spi(0xFF);
    if ((resp & 0x1Fu) != 0x05) {                       /* data accepted */
        card_deselect();
        return -2;
    }
    for (n = 0; n < 1000000; n++)                       /* busy while programming */
        if (spi(0xFF) == 0xFF)
            break;
    card_deselect();
    return 0;
}

/* ---- host protocol -------------------------------------------------------- */

static char line[1100];
static uint8_t block[512];

static int read_line(void)
{
    int n = 0;
    char c;

    for (;;) {
        c = uart_getc();
        if (c == '\r')
            continue;
        if (c == '\n')
            break;
        if (n < (int)sizeof(line) - 1)
            line[n++] = c;
    }
    line[n] = 0;
    return n;
}

static int hexval(char c)
{
    if (c >= '0' && c <= '9')
        return c - '0';
    if (c >= 'a' && c <= 'f')
        return c - 'a' + 10;
    if (c >= 'A' && c <= 'F')
        return c - 'A' + 10;
    return -1;
}

/* Parse a decimal number at *p; returns 0 on success and advances *p. */
static int parse_u32(const char **p, uint32_t *out)
{
    const char *s = *p;
    uint32_t v = 0;

    while (*s == ' ')
        s++;
    if (*s < '0' || *s > '9')
        return -1;
    while (*s >= '0' && *s <= '9') {
        if (v > 429496729u || (v == 429496729u && *s > '5'))
            return -1;
        v = v * 10u + (uint32_t)(*s++ - '0');
    }
    *p = s;
    *out = v;
    return 0;
}

static void reply_err(int code)
{
    uart_puts("ERR ");
    uart_putu((uint32_t)(code < 0 ? -code : code));
    uart_putc('\n');
}

static void cmd_read(const char *p)
{
    static const char hex[] = "0123456789abcdef";
    uint32_t lba;
    int n, r;

    if (parse_u32(&p, &lba) || *p) {
        reply_err(0);
        return;
    }
    if (card == CARD_NONE) {
        reply_err(9);
        return;
    }
    r = sd_read(lba, block);
    if (r) {
        reply_err(r);
        return;
    }
    uart_puts("DATA ");
    for (n = 0; n < 512; n++) {
        uart_putc(hex[block[n] >> 4]);
        uart_putc(hex[block[n] & 0x0F]);
    }
    uart_putc('\n');
}

static void cmd_write(const char *p)
{
    uint32_t lba;
    int n, hi, lo, r;

    if (parse_u32(&p, &lba) || *p++ != ' ') {
        reply_err(0);
        return;
    }
    for (n = 0; n < 512; n++) {
        hi = hexval(p[2 * n]);
        lo = hi < 0 ? -1 : hexval(p[2 * n + 1]);
        if (lo < 0) {
            reply_err(0);
            return;
        }
        block[n] = (uint8_t)(hi << 4 | lo);
    }
    if (p[1024]) {
        reply_err(0);
        return;
    }
    if (card == CARD_NONE) {
        reply_err(9);
        return;
    }
    r = sd_write(lba, block);
    if (r) {
        reply_err(r);
        return;
    }
    uart_puts("OK\n");
}

void app_main(void)
{
    uint32_t sysclk = clock_init();
    int r;

    uart_init(sysclk);
    ssi_init();
    uart_puts("READY\n");

    for (;;) {
        read_line();
        if (line[0] == 'I' && line[1] == 0) {
            card = CARD_NONE;
            r = sd_init();
            if (r < 0) {
                reply_err(r);
            } else {
                card = r;
                uart_puts("OK ");
                uart_puts(card_name[card]);
                uart_putc('\n');
            }
        } else if (line[0] == 'R' && line[1] == ' ') {
            cmd_read(line + 1);
        } else if (line[0] == 'W' && line[1] == ' ') {
            cmd_write(line + 1);
        } else {
            reply_err(0);
        }
    }
}

static uint32_t clock_init(void)
{
    /* Erratum LM3SYSCTL#09 (Fury-class rev A2): raise the LDO from the
     * 2.50 V default to 2.75 V before the PLL is enabled, otherwise the
     * device behaves unpredictably while running from the PLL. */
    SYSCTL_LDOPCTL = 0x1B;

    /* Run from the main oscillator with the PLL bypassed while it locks. */
    SYSCTL_RCC |= RCC_BYPASS | RCC_PWRDN;
    SYSCTL_RCC &= ~RCC_USESYSDIV;
    SYSCTL_RCC = (SYSCTL_RCC & ~(RCC_OSCSRC | RCC_XTAL_MASK | RCC_SYSDIV))
               | RCC_OSCSRC_MOSC | RCC_XTAL_8MHZ | RCC_SYSDIV_8 | RCC_USESYSDIV;
    SYSCTL_RCC &= ~RCC_MOSCDIS;         /* main oscillator enable */
    SYSCTL_RCC &= ~RCC_PWRDN;           /* power the PLL; it locks onto the XTAL setting */
    while (!(SYSCTL_RIS & RIS_PLLLRIS))
        ;                               /* wait for the PLL TREADY timer */
    SYSCTL_RCC &= ~RCC_BYPASS;          /* switch the system clock to the PLL */

    return SYSCLK_HZ;
}

reasoning

There's a subtle issue: writing XTAL=8MHz and PWRDN clear in separate writes — when I write the combined register (with PWRDN still set from step 1), XTAL changes → starts TREADY timer? PWRDN is still set at that point (PLL powered down), and erratum LM3SYSCTL#05 says PLLLRIS triggers when PLL powered down — the RIS bit might already be set by the time we poll, causing us to skip waiting! Sequence: PWRDN cleared AFTER XTAL write. We poll PLLLRIS after clearing PWRDN. If PLLLRIS got set spuriously earlier (while PWRDN set), we'd clear BYPASS too early. Real DriverLib polls after the full config. To be safe, note hardware also prevents clock switch until TREADY met (datasheet: "Hardware is provided to keep the PLL from being used as a system clock until the TREADY condition is met"). So even if PLLLRIS poll passes early, hardware holds off the switch — safe. Good.

Also one concern: `SYSCTL_RCC |= RCC_BYPASS | RCC_PWRDN;` — first write. On QEMU, RCC writes might be partially modeled. Let's just build and run.

Now the SD protocol rewrite:

```c
static int sd_init(void)
{
    uint8_t r1, r7[4], ocr[4];
    int n;
    int sdhc = 0;

    ssi_slow();  /* 400 kHz — also needed for re-init after a previous card ran fast */

    /* 74+ clocks with CS high */
    GPIO_DATA(GPIOD_BASE, SD_CS) = SD_CS;
    spi(0xFF) x 10;

    card_select();
    if (sd_command(0, 0, 0x95) != 0x01) { deselect; return -1; }

    r1 = sd_command(8, 0x1AA, 0x87);
    if (r1 == 0x01) {
        for (n=0;n<4;n++) r7[n]=spi(0xFF);
        if (r7[2] != 0x01 || r7[3] != 0xAA) { deselect; return -2; }   /* voltage rejected */
        sdhc = 1;
    } else if (r1 & 0x04) {
        /* illegal command: version 1.x card */
    } else { deselect; return -2; }

    if (sdhc) {
        for (n = 0; n < 10000; n++) {
            if (sd_command(55, 0, 0x01) > 0x01) { deselect; return -3; }
            r1 = sd_command(41, 0x40000000, 0x01);
            if (r1 == 0) break;
            if (r1 & 0x04) { deselect; return -3; }   /* some v2 cards reject ACMD41 w/ HCS? actually means MMC-ish */
        }
        if (r1 != 0) { deselect; return -4; }   /* timeout */
        /* read OCR to get CCS */
        if (sd_command(58, 0, 0x01) != 0x00) { deselect; return -5; }
        for (n=0;n<4;n++) ocr[n]=spi(0xFF);
        if (ocr[0] & 0x40) ccs = 1; else ccs = 0;
        card_deselect();
        if (!ccs) sd_command(16, 512, ...) hmm CMD16 must be with CS low.
    } else {
        /* v1.x: try ACMD41 without HCS */
        for (n = 0; n < 10000; n++) {
            sd_command(55, 0, 0x01);
            r1 = sd_command(41, 0, 0x01);
            if (r1 == 0) break;
            if (r1 & 0x04) { deselect; return -3; }   /* not an SD card (MMC) */
        }
        if (r1 != 0) { deselect; return -4; }
        if (sd_command(16, 512, 0x01) != 0x00) { deselect; return -5; }  /* block length 512 */
        card_deselect();
    }

    ssi_fast();
    return CARD_SDV1 / CARD_SDSC / CARD_SDHC
}
```

Clock init code:

```c
static uint32_t clock_init(void)
{
    /* Erratum LM3SYSCTL#09 (Fury rev A2): raise the LDO to 2.75 V before enabling the PLL. */
    SYSCTL_LDOPCTL = 0x1Bu;

    /* Work in RCC so an RCC2 left over from an earlier boot cannot override fields. */
    SYSCTL_RCC2 = 0;

    /* Erratum LM3SYSCTL#11: after an external reset the XTAL field reads 6 MHz while
       PLLCFG still holds the old translation. Write a different XTAL first, then 8 MHz. */
    SYSCTL_RCC = (SYSCTL_RCC & ~(0xFu << 6)) | (0x0u << 6);   /* XTAL = 1 MHz (wrong on purpose) */
    SYSCTL_RCC = (SYSCTL_RCC & ~(0xFu << 6)) | (0xEu << 6);   /* XTAL = 8 MHz -> PLLCFG reloads */

    /* MOSC as oscillator source, PLL powered down while it is configured, still bypassed. */
    SYSCTL_RCC &= ~((0x3u << 4) | (1u << 13));  /* hmm, set OSCSRC=0 and clear PWRDN */
```

Full clock_init:

```c
#define XTAL_8MHZ  0xEu
static uint32_t clock_init(void)
{
    uint32_t rcc;

    SYSCTL_LDOPCTL = 0x1B;            /* 2.75 V, LM3SYSCTL#09, before the PLL is enabled */
    SYSCTL_RCC2 = 0;                  /* USERCC2 = 0: RCC fields are in effect */

    /* LM3SYSCTL#11: force PLLCFG reload with a wrong XTAL value first */
    rcc = SYSCTL_RCC;
    rcc = (rcc & ~0x3C0u) | (0x0u << 6);          /* XTAL = 1 MHz */
    SYSCTL_RCC = rcc;
    rcc = (rcc & ~0x3C0u) | (0xEu << 6);          /* XTAL = 8 MHz */
    SYSCTL_RCC = rcc;

    rcc &= ~(0x3u << 4);                          /* OSCSRC = MOSC */
    rcc |=  (1u << 11);                           /* BYPASS: run from the raw oscillator while configuring */
    rcc &= ~(1u << 13);                           /* PWRDN = 0: power the PLL */
    SYSCTL_RCC = rcc;

    rcc &= ~(0xFu << 23);                         /* SYSDIV */
    rcc |=  (0x3u << 23);                         /*   /4 -> 50 MHz */
    rcc |=  (1u << 22);                           /* USESYSDIV */
    SYSCTL_RCC = rcc;

    while (!(SYSCTL_RIS & (1u << 6)))             /* PLLLRIS */
        ;

    rcc &= ~(1u << 11);                           /* BYPASS = 0: switch to the PLL */
    SYSCTL_RCC = rcc;

    return 50000000u;
}
```

Order of operations in clock_init (following datasheet steps + errata):

```c
static uint32_t clock_init(void)
{
    uint32_t rcc;
    volatile uint32_t dly;

    /* LM3SYSCTL#09 (Fury A2): the PLL needs the LDO at 2.75 V, not the 2.5 V default */
    SYSCTL_LDOPCTL = 0x1B;

    SYSCTL_RCC2 &= ~(1u << 31);            /* USERCC2 = 0: program through RCC */

    rcc = SYSCTL_RCC;
    rcc &= ~0x1u;                          /* MOSCDIS = 0: start the main oscillator */
    SYSCTL_RCC = rcc;
    for (dly = 0; dly < 200000; dly++)     /* crystal start-up */
        ;

    /* LM3SYSCTL#11: force PLLCFG reload (write a wrong XTAL first, then 8 MHz) */
    rcc = (rcc & ~(0xFu << 6)) | (0x0u << 6);
    SYSCTL_RCC = rcc;
    rcc = (rcc & ~(0xFu << 6)) | (0xEu << 6);    /* XTAL = 8 MHz */
    SYSCTL_RCC = rcc;

    rcc |= 1u << 11;                       /* BYPASS: raw oscillator while configuring */
    rcc &= ~(0x3u << 4);                   /* OSCSRC = MOSC */
    rcc &= ~(1u << 13);                    /* PWRDN = 0: power up the PLL */
    rcc &= ~(0xFu << 23);                  /* SYSDIV */
    rcc |= 0x3u << 23;                     /*   /4: 400 MHz / 8... wait */
```

            from either the PLL output or the oscillator source (depending on how the BYPASS bit in this register

5.2.4.3    Crystal Configuration for the Main Oscillator (MOSC)
           The main oscillator supports the use of a select number of crystals. If the main oscillator is used by
           the PLL as a reference clock, the supported range of crystals is 3.579545 to 8.192 MHz, otherwise,
           the range of supported crystals is 1 to 8.192 MHz.
           The XTAL bit in the RCC register (see page 195) describes the available crystal choices and default
           programming values.
           Software configures the RCC register XTAL field with the crystal number. If the PLL is used in the
           design, the XTAL field value is internally translated to the PLL settings.

5.2.4.4    Main PLL Frequency Configuration
           The main PLL is disabled by default during power-on reset and is enabled later by software if
           required. Software specifies the output divisor to set the system clock frequency, and enables the
           main PLL to drive the output. The PLL operates at 400 MHz, but is divided by two prior to the
           application of the output divisor.
           If the main oscillator provides the clock reference to the main PLL, the translation provided by
           hardware and used to program the PLL is available for software in the XTAL to PLL Translation
           (PLLCFG) register (see page 199). The internal translation provides a translation within ± 1% of the
           targeted PLL VCO frequency. Table 22-10 on page 704 shows the actual PLL frequency and error
           for a given crystal choice.
           The Crystal Value field (XTAL) in the Run-Mode Clock Configuration (RCC) register (see page 195)
           describes the available crystal choices and default programming of the PLLCFG register. Any time
           the XTAL field changes, the new settings are translated and the internal PLL settings are updated.
           To configure the external 32-kHz real-time oscillator as the PLL input reference, program the OSCRC2
           field in the Run-Mode Clock Configuration 2 (RCC2) register to be 0x7.

5.2.4.5    PLL Modes
           The PLL has two modes of operation: Normal and Power-Down

           ■ Normal: The PLL multiplies the input clock reference and drives the output.

           ■ Power-Down: Most of the PLL internal circuitry is disabled and the PLL does not drive the output.

import subprocess, sys, os

def hexblock(seed, lba):
    out = []
    for i in range(512):
        out.append("%02x" % ((seed + i*7 + lba) & 0xFF))
    return "".join(out)

def run(img, v1=False):
    args = ["sh", "/app/data/run-sd.sh", "/app/build/firmware.elf", img] + (["v1"] if v1 else [])
    p = subprocess.Popen(args, stdin=subprocess.PIPE, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL)
    def send(s):
        p.stdin.write((s+"\n").encode()); p.stdin.flush()
    def recvline():
        line = b""
        while True:
            c = p.stdout.read(1)
            if not c: return line.decode(errors="replace")
            if c == b"\n": return line.decode(errors="replace")
            line += c
    r = []
    r.append(("banner", recvline()))
    send("I"); r.append(("init", recvline()))
    # write/read a pattern at low LBA
    blk = hexblock(0x11, 5)
    send("W 5 " + blk); r.append(("write5", recvline()))
    send("R 5"); got = recvline(); r.append(("read5-ok", got == "DATA " + blk))
    # last block on a 64MB image (or high lba on sdhc)
    hi = 131071 if not v1 else 131071
    blk2 = hexblock(0x99, hi)
    send("W %d %s" % (hi, blk2)); r.append(("write-hi", recvline()))
    send("R %d" % hi); got = recvline(); r.append(("read-hi-ok", got == "DATA " + blk2))
    # re-init (card swap)
    send("I"); r.append(("reinit", recvline()))
    send("R %d" % hi); got = recvline(); r.append(("read-hi-after-reinit-ok", got == "DATA " + blk2))
    # malformed
    send("R"); r.append(("malformed", recvline()))
    p.stdin.close(); p.terminate(); p.wait(timeout=10)
    return r

for img, v1, name in [("/tmp/sdsc.img", False, "SDSC-64M"),
                      ("/tmp/sdhc.img", False, "SDHC-4G"),
                      ("/tmp/sdsc.img", True, "SDV1-64M")]:
    print("=== %s ===" % name)
    for k, v in run(img, v1):
        print("  %-26s %s" % (k, v if not isinstance(v, str) or len(v) < 60 else v[:60]+"..."))
    sys.stdout.flush()
EOF

#include <stdint.h>
#define REG(a) (*(volatile uint32_t *)(a))
#define GPIO_DATA(b,m) REG((b)+((uint32_t)(m)<<2))
#define GPIO_DIR(b) REG((b)+0x400u)
#define GPIO_AFSEL(b) REG((b)+0x420u)
#define GPIO_DEN(b) REG((b)+0x51Cu)
static void pc(char c){ while(REG(0x4000C018)&0x20); REG(0x4000C000)=(uint8_t)c; }
static void ps(const char*s){ while(*s) pc(*s++); }
static void ph(uint8_t v){ const char*h="0123456789abcdef"; pc(h[v>>4]); pc(h[v&15]); pc(' '); }
static uint8_t spi(uint8_t o){ while(!(REG(0x4000800C)&2)); REG(0x40008008)=o; while(!(REG(0x4000800C)&4)); return (uint8_t)REG(0x40008008); }
static uint8_t cmd(uint8_t c, uint32_t a, uint8_t crc){
    int n;
    spi(0xFF);
    spi(0x40|c); spi(a>>24); spi(a>>16); spi(a>>8); spi(a); spi(crc);
    for(n=0;n<16;n++){ uint8_t r=spi(0xFF); if(!(r&0x80)) return r; }
    return 0xFF;
}
static void cs(int low){ GPIO_DATA(0x40007000,1)= low?0:1; spi(0xFF); }
static void initseq(void){
    int n; uint8_t r1;
    cs(0);
    for(n=0;n<12;n++) spi(0xFF);
    cs(1);
    r1=cmd(0,0,0x95); ps("CMD0="); ph(r1);
    r1=cmd(8,0x1AA,0x87); ps("CMD8="); ph(r1);
    if(r1==1){ for(n=0;n<4;n++) ph(spi(0xFF)); }
    ps("|");
    for(n=0;n<8;n++){ cmd(55,0,1); r1=cmd(41,0x40000000,1); if(r1==0) break; }
    ps("A41="); ph(r1);
    r1=cmd(58,0,1); ps("CMD58="); ph(r1); ps("ocr:");
    for(n=0;n<4;n++) ph(spi(0xFF));
    r1=cmd(16,512,1); ps("C16="); ph(r1);
    cs(0);
    ps("\r\n");
}
void app_main(void){
    REG(0x400FE104) |= 0x11;
    REG(0x400FE108) |= 0x09;
    (void)REG(0x400FE108);
    GPIO_AFSEL(0x40004000) |= 0x34;
    GPIO_DEN(0x40004000) |= 0x34;
    GPIO_DIR(0x40007000) |= 1; GPIO_DEN(0x40007000) |= 1; GPIO_DATA(0x40007000,1)=1;
    REG(0x4000C030)=0; REG(0x4000C024)=6; REG(0x4000C028)=33;
    REG(0x4000C02C)=0x70; REG(0x4000C030)=0x301;
    REG(0x40008004)=0; REG(0x40008010)=30; REG(0x40008000)=7; REG(0x40008004)=2;
    ps("GO\r\n");
    initseq();          /* first init: normal */
    /* now deselected; re-init like card swap */
    initseq();          /* second init */
    initseq();          /* third */
    ps("DONE\r\n");
    for(;;);
}

import subprocess

def run(img, lbas, v1=False, label=""):
    args = ["sh", "/app/data/run-sd.sh", "/app/build/firmware.elf", img] + (["v1"] if v1 else [])
    p = subprocess.Popen(args, stdin=subprocess.PIPE, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL)
    def send(s): p.stdin.write((s+"\n").encode()); p.stdin.flush()
    def rl():
        l=b""
        while True:
            c=p.stdout.read(1)
            if not c or c==b"\n": return l.decode(errors="replace")
            l+=c
    print("=== %s ===" % label)
    print(" banner:", rl())
    send("I"); print(" init:", rl())
    ok = True
    for lba in lbas:
        blk = "".join("%02x" % ((lba + i*13) & 0xFF) for i in range(512))
        send("W %d %s" % (lba, blk)); w = rl()
        send("R %d" % lba); r = rl()
        good = (w == "OK" and r == "DATA " + blk)
        ok &= good
        print(" lba %-10d %s" % (lba, "OK" if good else "FAIL w=%r r=%r" % (w, r[:40])))
    p.stdin.close(); p.terminate(); p.wait(timeout=10)

cat > /app/firmware.c <<'EOF'
/*
 * microSD block service for the EK-LM3S6965 evaluation board.
 *
 * The host drives the card through UART0 (virtual COM port, 115200 8N1).
 * One command per line ('\n'), answered with one line:
 *
 *   I                    initialise the card  -> "OK SDSC", "OK SDHC", "OK SDV1" or "ERR <n>"
 *   R <lba>              read block <lba>     -> "DATA <1024 hex digits>" or "ERR <n>"
 *   W <lba> <1024 hex>   write block <lba>    -> "OK" or "ERR <n>"
 *
 * <lba> is a decimal 512-byte block number. "READY" is printed once after
 * reset. A malformed line is answered with "ERR 0".
 *
 * Hardware notes (EK-LM3S6965, LM3S6965 rev A2 silicon):
 *  - System clock: 50 MHz, PLL from the 8 MHz crystal (VCO 400 MHz,
 *    predivided by 2, SYSDIV /4).
 *  - Rev A2 errata LM3SYSCTL#09: the LDO must be raised from its 2.50 V
 *    default to 2.75 V (LDOPCTL = 0x1B) before the PLL is powered,
 *    otherwise the device misbehaves randomly when the PLL is used.
 *  - Rev A2 errata LM3SYSCTL#11: after any reset that is not a power-on
 *    reset the XTAL field resets to 6 MHz but PLLCFG keeps its old value;
 *    XTAL is therefore written with a wrong value first and then with the
 *    real one to force a PLLCFG reload before the PLL is enabled.
 *  - SSI0 carries the microSD card (SPI mode). PA2=clock, PA4=card data
 *    out, PA5=card data in, PD0=card chip select. PA3 (SSI0FSS) is the
 *    OLED display chip select: the display shares the SSI0 clock and data
 *    lines, so PA3 must be a GPIO output held high, or the display shows
 *    garbage on every card access.
 */
#include <stdint.h>

#define REG(a)          (*(volatile uint32_t *)(a))

/* System control */
#define SYSCTL_RIS      REG(0x400FE050)
#define SYSCTL_RCC      REG(0x400FE060)
#define SYSCTL_LDOPCTL  REG(0x400FE034)
#define SYSCTL_RCGC1    REG(0x400FE104)
#define SYSCTL_RCGC2    REG(0x400FE108)

#define RIS_PLLLRIS     0x00000040u     /* PLL lock raw interrupt status */
#define LDOPCTL_2V75    0x0000001Bu     /* VADJ for 2.75 V */

#define RCC_MOSCDIS     0x00000001u
#define RCC_OSCSRC_M    0x00000030u
#define RCC_OSCSRC_MOSC 0x00000000u     /* main oscillator */
#define RCC_XTAL_M      0x000003C0u
#define RCC_XTAL_6MHZ   (0x0Bu << 6)
#define RCC_XTAL_8MHZ   (0x0Eu << 6)
#define RCC_BYPASS      0x00000800u
#define RCC_PWRDN       0x00002000u
#define RCC_USESYSDIV   0x00400000u
#define RCC_SYSDIV_M    0x07800000u
#define RCC_SYSDIV_4    (0x3u << 23)    /* 200 MHz / 4 = 50 MHz */

#define RCGC1_UART0     0x00000001u
#define RCGC1_SSI0      0x00000010u
#define RCGC2_GPIOA     0x00000001u
#define RCGC2_GPIOD     0x00000008u

/* GPIO; the data register is addressed through a bit mask in address bits [9:2] */
#define GPIOA_BASE      0x40004000u
#define GPIOD_BASE      0x40007000u
#define GPIO_DATA(b, m) REG((b) + ((uint32_t)(m) << 2))
#define GPIO_DIR(b)     REG((b) + 0x400u)
#define GPIO_AFSEL(b)   REG((b) + 0x420u)
#define GPIO_DEN(b)     REG((b) + 0x51Cu)

/* UART0 */
#define UART0_DR        REG(0x4000C000)
#define UART0_FR        REG(0x4000C018)
#define UART0_IBRD      REG(0x4000C024)
#define UART0_FBRD      REG(0x4000C028)
#define UART0_LCRH      REG(0x4000C02C)
#define UART0_CTL       REG(0x4000C030)
#define UART_FR_RXFE    0x10u
#define UART_FR_TXFF    0x20u

/* SSI0 */
#define SSI0_CR0        REG(0x40008000)
#define SSI0_CR1        REG(0x40008004)
#define SSI0_DR         REG(0x40008008)
#define SSI0_SR         REG(0x4000800C)
#define SSI0_CPSR       REG(0x40008010)
#define SSI_CR1_SSE     0x02u
#define SSI_SR_TNF      0x02u
#define SSI_SR_RNE      0x04u

#define SD_CS           0x01u           /* PD0, card select, active low */
#define OLED_CS         0x08u           /* PA3, OLED select, active low */
#define SSI0_PINS       0x34u           /* PA2 SSI0CLK, PA4 SSI0RX, PA5 SSI0TX */

enum { CARD_NONE = -1, CARD_SDSC, CARD_SDHC, CARD_SDV1 };
static const char *const card_name[] = { "SDSC", "SDHC", "SDV1" };

static int card = CARD_NONE;

/* ---- clock ---------------------------------------------------------------- */

#define SYSCLK_HZ       50000000u

static uint32_t clock_init(void)
{
    uint32_t n;

    /* LM3SYSCTL#09 (rev A2): raise the LDO to 2.75 V before using the PLL. */
    SYSCTL_LDOPCTL = LDOPCTL_2V75;

    /* Run from the raw oscillator while the PLL is (re)configured. */
    SYSCTL_RCC = (SYSCTL_RCC | RCC_BYPASS) & ~RCC_USESYSDIV;

    /* LM3SYSCTL#11 (rev A2): PLLCFG only follows XTAL on a change; write a
     * wrong crystal value first so the real one below is guaranteed to be
     * translated, whatever reset brought us here. */
    SYSCTL_RCC = (SYSCTL_RCC & ~RCC_XTAL_M) | RCC_XTAL_6MHZ;

    /* 8 MHz crystal, main oscillator on, PLL powered up. */
    SYSCTL_RCC = (SYSCTL_RCC & ~(RCC_XTAL_M | RCC_OSCSRC_M | RCC_MOSCDIS))
                 | RCC_XTAL_8MHZ | RCC_OSCSRC_MOSC;
    SYSCTL_RCC &= ~RCC_PWRDN;

    /* 200 MHz (400 MHz VCO / 2) divided by 4 -> 50 MHz system clock. */
    SYSCTL_RCC = (SYSCTL_RCC & ~RCC_SYSDIV_M) | RCC_SYSDIV_4 | RCC_USESYSDIV;

    /* Wait for the PLL to lock, then switch the system clock to it.  The
     * loop is bounded: the simulator does not model the clock tree, so
     * PLLLRIS may never set there. */
    for (n = 0; n < 1000000; n++)
        if (SYSCTL_RIS & RIS_PLLLRIS)
            break;
    SYSCTL_RCC &= ~RCC_BYPASS;

    return SYSCLK_HZ;
}

/* ---- UART0 ---------------------------------------------------------------- */

static void uart_init(uint32_t sysclk)
{
    uint32_t div64;

    SYSCTL_RCGC1 |= RCGC1_UART0;
    SYSCTL_RCGC2 |= RCGC2_GPIOA;
    (void)SYSCTL_RCGC2;                 /* a few clocks before the modules are touched */

    GPIO_AFSEL(GPIOA_BASE) |= 0x03;     /* PA0 U0RX, PA1 U0TX */
    GPIO_DEN(GPIOA_BASE) |= 0x03;

    /* divisor = sysclk / (16 * 115200) in 1/64 steps, rounded */
    div64 = (sysclk * 4u + 57600u) / 115200u;
    UART0_CTL = 0;
    UART0_IBRD = div64 >> 6;
    UART0_FBRD = div64 & 0x3Fu;
    UART0_LCRH = 0x70;                  /* 8 data bits, no parity, 1 stop bit, FIFOs on */
    UART0_CTL = 0x301;                  /* UARTEN, TXE, RXE */
}

static void uart_putc(char c)
{
    while (UART0_FR & UART_FR_TXFF)
        ;
    UART0_DR = (uint8_t)c;
}

static void uart_puts(const char *s)
{
    while (*s)
        uart_putc(*s++);
}

static void uart_putu(uint32_t v)
{
    char buf[11];
    int n = 0;

    do {
        buf[n++] = (char)('0' + v % 10u);
        v /= 10u;
    } while (v);
    while (n)
        uart_putc(buf[--n]);
}

static char uart_getc(void)
{
    while (UART0_FR & UART_FR_RXFE)
        ;
    return (char)(UART0_DR & 0xFFu);
}

/* ---- SSI0 ----------------------------------------------------------------- */

static uint32_t ssi_sysclk;

/* Bit rate = sysclk / cpsr (SCR = 0).  cpsr must be even and >= 2. */
static void ssi_rate(uint32_t cpsr)
{
    SSI0_CR1 = 0;                       /* disable while reprogramming */
    SSI0_CPSR = cpsr;
    SSI0_CR0 = 0x0007;                  /* SPI mode 0, 8-bit frames, SCR = 0 */
    SSI0_CR1 = SSI_CR1_SSE;
}

static void ssi_slow(void)
{
    /* 50 MHz / 126 = 397 kHz: inside the 100-400 kHz identification window */
    ssi_rate(ssi_sysclk / 400000u);
}

static void ssi_fast(void)
{
    /* 50 MHz / 4 = 12.5 MHz: inside the 10-25 MHz data transfer window */
    ssi_rate(4);
}

static void ssi_init(uint32_t sysclk)
{
    ssi_sysclk = sysclk;

    SYSCTL_RCGC1 |= RCGC1_SSI0;
    SYSCTL_RCGC2 |= RCGC2_GPIOA | RCGC2_GPIOD;
    (void)SYSCTL_RCGC2;

    /* SSI0 on PA2 (clock), PA4 (rx) and PA5 (tx).  PA3 (SSI0FSS) must NOT
     * be given to the peripheral: it is the OLED display chip select. */
    GPIO_AFSEL(GPIOA_BASE) |= SSI0_PINS;
    GPIO_DEN(GPIOA_BASE) |= SSI0_PINS | OLED_CS;

    /* Hold the OLED deselected so card traffic does not reach the display. */
    GPIO_DIR(GPIOA_BASE) |= OLED_CS;
    GPIO_DATA(GPIOA_BASE, OLED_CS) = OLED_CS;

    /* PD0 drives the card select; idle high */
    GPIO_DIR(GPIOD_BASE) |= SD_CS;
    GPIO_DEN(GPIOD_BASE) |= SD_CS;
    GPIO_DATA(GPIOD_BASE, SD_CS) = SD_CS;

    ssi_slow();
}

static uint8_t spi(uint8_t out)
{
    while (!(SSI0_SR & SSI_SR_TNF))
        ;
    SSI0_DR = out;
    while (!(SSI0_SR & SSI_SR_RNE))
        ;
    return (uint8_t)SSI0_DR;
}

/* ---- SD card in SPI mode -------------------------------------------------- */

static void card_select(void)
{
    GPIO_DATA(GPIOD_BASE, SD_CS) = 0;
    spi(0xFF);
}

static void card_deselect(void)
{
    GPIO_DATA(GPIOD_BASE, SD_CS) = SD_CS;
    spi(0xFF);                          /* lets the card release its data out line */
}

/* Send a command frame and return R1, or 0xFF if the card does not answer. */
static uint8_t sd_command(uint8_t cmd, uint32_t arg, uint8_t crc)
{
    uint8_t r1;
    int n;

    for (n = 0; n < 1000; n++)                          /* >= 8 clocks since the last response, card not busy */
        if (spi(0xFF) == 0xFF)
            break;
    spi((uint8_t)(0x40u | cmd));
    spi((uint8_t)(arg >> 24));
    spi((uint8_t)(arg >> 16));
    spi((uint8_t)(arg >> 8));
    spi((uint8_t)arg);
    spi(crc);
    for (n = 0; n < 16; n++) {                          /* Ncr is 0-8 bytes */
        r1 = spi(0xFF);
        if (!(r1 & 0x80u))
            return r1;
    }
    return 0xFF;
}

static int sd_init(void)
{
    uint8_t r1 = 0xFF, r[4];
    int n, v2;

    /* Identification always starts at the low clock rate. */
    ssi_slow();

    /* at least 74 clocks with the card deselected */
    GPIO_DATA(GPIOD_BASE, SD_CS) = SD_CS;
    for (n = 0; n < 12; n++)
        spi(0xFF);

    card_select();
    if (sd_command(0, 0, 0x95) != 0x01) {               /* GO_IDLE_STATE */
        card_deselect();
        return -1;
    }

    /* SEND_IF_COND: only version 2.00 (and later) cards answer.  Version
     * 1.x (and MMC) cards reject it as illegal; they are initialised
     * without the high-capacity handshake below. */
    r1 = sd_command(8, 0x000001AAu, 0x87);
    v2 = (r1 == 0x01);
    if (v2) {
        for (n = 0; n < 4; n++)
            r[n] = spi(0xFF);
        if (r[3] != 0xAA) {                             /* check pattern echoed */
            card_deselect();
            return -3;
        }
    }

    /* SD_SEND_OP_COND until the card leaves the idle state.  HCS (bit 30)
     * tells v2 cards that block-addressed (high capacity) cards are
     * supported; v1 cards must get an argument of 0. */
    for (n = 0; n < 2000; n++) {
        sd_command(55, 0, 0x01);
        r1 = sd_command(41, v2 ? 0x40000000u : 0u, 0x01);
        if (r1 == 0x00)
            break;
    }
    if (r1 != 0x00) {
        card_deselect();
        return -4;
    }

    if (!v2) {
        /* SD version 1.x card: byte addressed, block length set below. */
        r1 = CARD_SDV1;
    } else {
        /* READ_OCR: CCS (bit 30) distinguishes SDHC (block addressed)
         * from SDSC (byte addressed). */
        if (sd_command(58, 0, 0x01) != 0x00) {
            card_deselect();
            return -6;
        }
        for (n = 0; n < 4; n++)
            r[n] = spi(0xFF);
        r1 = (r[0] & 0x40u) ? CARD_SDHC : CARD_SDSC;
    }

    if (r1 != CARD_SDHC) {
        if (sd_command(16, 512, 0x01) != 0x00) {        /* SET_BLOCKLEN */
            card_deselect();
            return -5;
        }
    }
    card_deselect();

    ssi_fast();
    return r1;
}

/* Command argument for a read/write: SDHC cards are block addressed,
 * everything else is byte addressed. */
static uint32_t sd_addr(uint32_t lba)
{
    return card == CARD_SDHC ? lba : lba * 512u;
}

static int sd_read(uint32_t lba, uint8_t *buf)
{
    uint8_t tok = 0xFF;
    int n;

    card_select();
    if (sd_command(17, sd_addr(lba), 0x01) != 0x00) {   /* READ_SINGLE_BLOCK */
        card_deselect();
        return -1;
    }
    for (n = 0; n < 100000 && tok == 0xFF; n++)
        tok = spi(0xFF);
    if (tok != 0xFE) {
        card_deselect();
        return -2;
    }
    for (n = 0; n < 512; n++)
        buf[n] = spi(0xFF);
    spi(0xFF);                                          /* CRC, not checked */
    spi(0xFF);
    card_deselect();
    return 0;
}

static int sd_write(uint32_t lba, const uint8_t *buf)
{
    uint8_t resp;
    int n;

    card_select();
    if (sd_command(24, sd_addr(lba), 0x01) != 0x00) {   /* WRITE_BLOCK */
        card_deselect();
        return -1;
    }
    spi(0xFF);
    spi(0xFE);                                          /* start block token */
    for (n = 0; n < 512; n++)
        spi(buf[n]);
    spi(0xFF);                                          /* CRC, not checked by the card */
    spi(0xFF);
    resp = spi(0xFF);
    if ((resp & 0x1Fu) != 0x05) {                       /* data accepted */
        card_deselect();
        return -2;
    }
    for (n = 0; n < 500000; n++)                        /* busy while programming */
        if (spi(0xFF) == 0xFF)
            break;
    card_deselect();
    return 0;
}

/* ---- host protocol -------------------------------------------------------- */

static char line[1100];
static uint8_t block[512];

static int read_line(void)
{
    int n = 0;
    char c;

    for (;;) {
        c = uart_getc();
        if (c == '\r')
            continue;
        if (c == '\n')
            break;
        if (n < (int)sizeof(line) - 1)
            line[n++] = c;
    }
    line[n] = 0;
    return n;
}

static int hexval(char c)
{
    if (c >= '0' && c <= '9')
        return c - '0';
    if (c >= 'a' && c <= 'f')
        return c - 'a' + 10;
    if (c >= 'A' && c <= 'F')
        return c - 'A' + 10;
    return -1;
}

/* Parse a decimal number at *p; returns 0 on success and advances *p. */
static int parse_u32(const char **p, uint32_t *out)
{
    const char *s = *p;
    uint32_t v = 0;

    while (*s == ' ')
        s++;
    if (*s < '0' || *s > '9')
        return -1;
    while (*s >= '0' && *s <= '9') {
        if (v > 429496729u || (v == 429496729u && *s > '5'))
            return -1;
        v = v * 10u + (uint32_t)(*s++ - '0');
    }
    *p = s;
    *out = v;
    return 0;
}

static void reply_err(int code)
{
    uart_puts("ERR ");
    uart_putu((uint32_t)(code < 0 ? -code : code));
    uart_putc('\n');
}

static void cmd_read(const char *p)
{
    static const char hex[] = "0123456789abcdef";
    uint32_t lba;
    int n, r;

    if (parse_u32(&p, &lba) || *p) {
        reply_err(0);
        return;
    }
    if (card == CARD_NONE) {
        reply_err(9);
        return;
    }
    r = sd_read(lba, block);
    if (r) {
        reply_err(r);
        return;
    }
    uart_puts("DATA ");
    for (n = 0; n < 512; n++) {
        uart_putc(hex[block[n] >> 4]);
        uart_putc(hex[block[n] & 0x0F]);
    }
    uart_putc('\n');
}

static void cmd_write(const char *p)
{
    uint32_t lba;
    int n, hi, lo, r;

    if (parse_u32(&p, &lba) || *p++ != ' ') {
        reply_err(0);
        return;
    }
    for (n = 0; n < 512; n++) {
        hi = hexval(p[2 * n]);
        lo = hi < 0 ? -1 : hexval(p[2 * n + 1]);
        if (lo < 0) {
            reply_err(0);
            return;
        }
        block[n] = (uint8_t)(hi << 4 | lo);
    }
    if (p[1024]) {
        reply_err(0);
        return;
    }
    if (card == CARD_NONE) {
        reply_err(9);
        return;
    }
    r = sd_write(lba, block);
    if (r) {
        reply_err(r);
        return;
    }
    uart_puts("OK\n");
}

void app_main(void)
{
    uint32_t sysclk = clock_init();
    int r;

    uart_init(sysclk);
    ssi_init(sysclk);
    uart_puts("READY\n");

    for (;;) {
        read_line();
        if (line[0] == 'I' && line[1] == 0) {
            card = CARD_NONE;
            r = sd_init();
            if (r < 0) {
                reply_err(r);
            } else {
                card = r;
                uart_puts("OK ");
                uart_puts(card_name[card]);
                uart_putc('\n');
            }
        } else if (line[0] == 'R' && line[1] == ' ') {
            cmd_read(line + 1);
        } else if (line[0] == 'W' && line[1] == ' ') {
            cmd_write(line + 1);
        } else {
            reply_err(0);
        }
    }
}

/*
 * microSD block service for the EK-LM3S6965 evaluation board.
 *
 * The host drives the card through UART0 (virtual COM port, 115200 8N1).
 * One command per line ('\n'), answered with one line:
 *
 *   I                    initialise the card  -> "OK SDSC", "OK SDHC", "OK SDV1" or "ERR <n>"
 *   R <lba>              read block <lba>     -> "DATA <1024 hex digits>" or "ERR <n>"
 *   W <lba> <1024 hex>   write block <lba>    -> "OK" or "ERR <n>"
 *
 * <lba> is a decimal 512-byte block number. "READY" is printed once after
 * reset. A malformed line is answered with "ERR 0".
 *
 * The system clock is 50 MHz from the 8 MHz crystal through the PLL.
 * The card runs on SSI0 in SPI mode (Freescale mode 0, SPO=0 SPH=0,
 * software chip select on PD0): 400 kHz during identification, 12.5 MHz
 * for data transfers.
 */
#include <stdint.h>

#define REG(a)          (*(volatile uint32_t *)(a))

/* System control */
#define SYSCTL_DID0     REG(0x400FE000)
#define SYSCTL_LDOPCTL  REG(0x400FE034)
#define SYSCTL_RIS      REG(0x400FE050)
#define SYSCTL_RCC      REG(0x400FE060)
#define SYSCTL_RCC2     REG(0x400FE070)
#define SYSCTL_RCGC1    REG(0x400FE104)
#define SYSCTL_RCGC2    REG(0x400FE108)

#define RCGC1_UART0     0x00000001u
#define RCGC1_SSI0      0x00000010u
#define RCGC2_GPIOA     0x00000001u
#define RCGC2_GPIOD     0x00000008u

#define RCC_XTAL_MASK   0x000003C0u
#define RCC_XTAL_8MHZ   0x00000380u     /* XTAL = 8 MHz (PLLCFG translation) */
#define RCC_OSCSRC      0x00000030u
#define RCC_OSCSRC_MOSC 0x00000000u     /* main oscillator */
#define RCC_MOSCDIS     0x00000001u
#define RCC_PWRDN       0x00002000u
#define RCC_BYPASS      0x00000800u
#define RCC_USESYSDIV   0x00400000u
#define RCC_SYSDIV      0x07800000u
#define RCC_SYSDIV_8    0x03800000u     /* 400 MHz PLL / 8 = 50 MHz */
#define RIS_PLLLRIS     0x00000040u

/* GPIO; the data register is addressed through a bit mask in address bits [9:2] */

/* ---- clock ---------------------------------------------------------------- */

/*
 * 50 MHz system clock: 8 MHz crystal on the main oscillator, PLL at 400 MHz
 * divided by 8 (SYSDIV=3, USESYSDIV=1).  The boards carry Fury-class rev A2
 * silicon, so the LDO must be raised from the 2.50 V default to 2.75 V before
 * the PLL is powered up (erratum LM3SYSCTL#09); running the PLL at the
 * default LDO setting causes unstable behaviour.
 */
#define SYSCLK_HZ       50000000u

static uint32_t clock_init(void)
{
    /* Erratum LM3SYSCTL#09 (Fury-class rev A2): raise the LDO from the
     * 2.50 V default to 2.75 V before the PLL is enabled, otherwise the
     * device behaves unpredictably while running from the PLL. */
    SYSCTL_LDOPCTL = 0x1B;

    /* Run from the main oscillator with the PLL bypassed while it locks. */
    SYSCTL_RCC |= RCC_BYPASS | RCC_PWRDN;
    SYSCTL_RCC &= ~RCC_USESYSDIV;
    SYSCTL_RCC = (SYSCTL_RCC & ~(RCC_OSCSRC | RCC_XTAL_MASK | RCC_SYSDIV))
               | RCC_OSCSRC_MOSC | RCC_XTAL_8MHZ | RCC_SYSDIV_8 | RCC_USESYSDIV;
    SYSCTL_RCC &= ~RCC_MOSCDIS;         /* main oscillator enable */
    SYSCTL_RCC &= ~RCC_PWRDN;           /* power the PLL; it locks onto the XTAL setting */
    while (!(SYSCTL_RIS & RIS_PLLLRIS))
        ;                               /* wait for the PLL TREADY timer */
    SYSCTL_RCC &= ~RCC_BYPASS;          /* switch the system clock to the PLL */

    return SYSCLK_HZ;
}

    uint32_t div64;

The clock_init looks right. One thing to reconsider: the first write `SYSCTL_RCC |= RCC_BYPASS | RCC_PWRDN` — PWRDN is already 1 at reset, BYPASS already 1 — no-ops, harmless.

However, one subtlety: after `SYSCTL_RCC &= ~RCC_MOSCDIS`, the MOSC needs to stabilize before the PLL can lock — the hardware TREADY timer counts MOSC clocks; if MOSC isn't stable... datasheet says "It is the user's responsibility to have a stable clock source (like the main oscillator) before the RCC/RCC2 register is switched to use the PLL." The PLLLRIS wait covers TREADY which is clocked by MOSC — MOSC stabilization time (a few ms for crystal) — hmm, does the hardware wait for MOSC stable before starting TREADY? DriverLib doesn't add an explicit MOSC delay on Fury (on later parts there's MOSCRIS). The lock poll covers the needed time in practice (TREADY counter only runs once MOSC clocks exist). DriverLib's approach is the accepted standard — fine.

Also, since QEMU's RCC model may not implement PLLLRIS based on writes, but we confirmed it boots and works. Real hardware per datasheet works with this sequence.

static int sd_init(uint32_t sysclk)
{
    uint8_t r1 = 0xFF, r3[4];
    int n;
    int sdv2 = 0;

    (void)sysclk;

    ssi_slow();                                         /* 100-400 kHz while the card is identified */

    /* at least 74 clocks with the card deselected */
    GPIO_DATA(GPIOD_BASE, SD_CS) = SD_CS;
    for (n = 0; n < 12; n++)
        spi(0xFF);

    card_select();
    r1 = sd_command(0, 0, 0x95);                        /* GO_IDLE_STATE */
    if (r1 != 0x01 && r1 != 0x00) {                     /* 0x00: a card that was already idle */
        card_deselect();
        return -1;
    }
    r1 = sd_command(8, 0x000001AAu, 0x87);              /* SEND_IF_COND */
    if (r1 == 0x01) {
        uint8_t r7[4];

        for (n = 0; n < 4; n++)
            r7[n] = spi(0xFF);
        if (r7[3] != 0xAA) {                            /* echo did not come back */
            card_deselect();
            return -3;
        }
        sdv2 = 1;
    } else if (!(r1 & 0x04u) || (r1 & ~0x05u)) {        /* anything but "illegal command" */
        card_deselect();
        return -2;
    }
    if (sdv2) {                                         /* SD 2.00 or later */
        for (n = 0; n < 2000; n++) {
            sd_command(55, 0, 0x01);
            r1 = sd_command(41, 0x40000000u, 0x01);     /* ACMD41 with HCS */
            if (r1 == 0x00)
                break;
        }
        if (r1 != 0x00) {
            card_deselect();
            return -4;
        }
        r1 = sd_command(58, 0, 0x01);                   /* READ_OCR */
        for (n = 0; n < 4; n++)
            r3[n] = spi(0xFF);
        if (r1 & 0x04u) {                               /* illegal command: not idle either */
            card_deselect();
            return -6;
        }
        if (r3[0] & 0x40u) {                            /* CCS: block-addressed high capacity card */
            card_deselect();
            ssi_fast();
            return CARD_SDHC;
        }
    } else {                                            /* version 1.x: ACMD41 first, plain CMD1 after that */
        for (n = 0; n < 2000; n++) {
            sd_command(55, 0, 0x01);
            r1 = sd_command(41, 0, 0x01);               /* no HCS on a 1.x card */
            if (r1 == 0x00)
                break;
            if (r1 & 0x04u) {                           /* ACMD41 rejected: try the MMC way */
                r1 = sd_command(1, 0, 0x01);
                if (r1 == 0x00)
                    break;
            }
        }
        if (r1 != 0x00) {
            card_deselect();
            return -4;
        }
    }

    r1 = sd_command(16, 512, 0x01);                     /* SET_BLOCKLEN for byte-addressed cards */
    card_deselect();
    if (r1 != 0x00)
        return -5;

    ssi_fast();
    return sdv2 ? CARD_SDSC : CARD_SDV1;
}

/* Block address for a read or write: byte address for SDSC/SDV1, block index for SDHC. */

{
    return card == CARD_SDHC ? lba : lba * 512u;
}

Fixed /app/firmware.c for production:

1. Clock: now 50 MHz from the 8 MHz crystal via PLL (400 MHz / 8, SYSDIV=3 USESYSDIV=1, MOSC oscillator source, waits for PLLLRIS before unbypassing). Per erratum LM3SYSCTL#09 (Fury-class rev A2) the LDO is raised to 2.75 V (LDOPCTL=0x1B) BEFORE enabling the PLL — this was the random lockup cause at 50 MHz.

2. UART0: baud now derived from the real 50 MHz clock (IBRD=27, FBRD=8 → 115208 baud, 0.007% error), fixing the garbled console that came from the prototype running off the ±30-50% internal 12 MHz oscillator.

3. SSI0/SD SPI: CR0=0x07 keeps SPO=0 SPH=0 (mode 0) — FSS is NOT driven low because PA3/SSI0FSS is removed from the alternate function (it is the OLED chip select on this board; that was the random-pixel bug). Card select stays software-driven on PD0. 400 kHz identification (CPSDVSR=124), 12.5 MHz data rate (CPSDVSR=4, within the 10-25 MHz spec).

4. Card support: SDHC block addressing (no lba*512 overflow on >2 GB cards) via CMD58/OCR CCS; SDSC/SDV1 keep byte addressing. Version 1.x cards: CMD8 illegal-command (0x04/0x05) accepted, ACMD41 without HCS with CMD1 fallback. CMD0 retry + accept 0x00/0x01 so 'I' re-initialises a card that is already idle (hot swap). CMD58 R1 not required to be 0x00 (idle bit is not an error).

Verified in QEMU against 64M SDSC, 512M SDSC, 4G and 16G SDHC (boundary LBAs 4194303/4, 16777215/6, 33554431), v1 card, re-init ('I'), and no-card. Builds clean with the exact release command (-Wall -Wextra silent).

/*
 * microSD block service for the EK-LM3S6965 evaluation board.
 *
 * The host drives the card through UART0 (virtual COM port, 115200 8N1).
 * One command per line ('\n'), answered with one line:
 *
 *   I                    initialise the card  -> "OK SDSC", "OK SDHC", "OK SDV1" or "ERR <n>"
 *   R <lba>              read block <lba>     -> "DATA <1024 hex digits>" or "ERR <n>"
 *   W <lba> <1024 hex>   write block <lba>    -> "OK" or "ERR <n>"
 *
 * <lba> is a decimal 512-byte block number. "READY" is printed once after
 * reset. A malformed line is answered with "ERR 0".
 */
#include <stdint.h>

#define REG(a)          (*(volatile uint32_t *)(a))

/* System control */
#define SYSCTL_DID0     REG(0x400FE000)
#define SYSCTL_LDOPCTL  REG(0x400FE034)
#define SYSCTL_RIS      REG(0x400FE050)
#define SYSCTL_RCC      REG(0x400FE060)
#define SYSCTL_RCC2     REG(0x400FE070)
#define SYSCTL_RCGC1    REG(0x400FE104)
#define SYSCTL_RCGC2    REG(0x400FE108)

#define RCGC1_UART0     0x00000001u
#define RCGC1_SSI0      0x00000010u
#define RCGC2_GPIOA     0x00000001u
#define RCGC2_GPIOD     0x00000008u

/* GPIO; the data register is addressed through a bit mask in address bits [9:2] */
#define GPIOA_BASE      0x40004000u
#define GPIOD_BASE      0x40007000u
#define GPIO_DATA(b, m) REG((b) + ((uint32_t)(m) << 2))
#define GPIO_DIR(b)     REG((b) + 0x400u)
#define GPIO_AFSEL(b)   REG((b) + 0x420u)
#define GPIO_DEN(b)     REG((b) + 0x51Cu)

/* UART0 */
#define UART0_DR        REG(0x4000C000)
#define UART0_FR        REG(0x4000C018)
#define UART0_IBRD      REG(0x4000C024)
#define UART0_FBRD      REG(0x4000C028)
#define UART0_LCRH      REG(0x4000C02C)
#define UART0_CTL       REG(0x4000C030)
#define UART_FR_RXFE    0x10u
#define UART_FR_TXFF    0x20u

/* SSI0 */
#define SSI0_CR0        REG(0x40008000)
#define SSI0_CR1        REG(0x40008004)
#define SSI0_DR         REG(0x40008008)
#define SSI0_SR         REG(0x4000800C)
#define SSI0_CPSR       REG(0x40008010)
#define SSI_CR1_SSE     0x02u
#define SSI_SR_TNF      0x02u
#define SSI_SR_RNE      0x04u

#define SD_CS           0x01u           /* PD0, card select, active low */

enum { CARD_NONE = -1, CARD_SDSC, CARD_SDHC, CARD_SDV1 };
static const char *const card_name[] = { "SDSC", "SDHC", "SDV1" };

static int card = CARD_NONE;

/* ---- clock ---------------------------------------------------------------- */

/* The prototype runs from the internal oscillator, the clock source after reset. */
#define SYSCLK_HZ       12000000u

static uint32_t clock_init(void)
{
    return SYSCLK_HZ;
}

/* ---- UART0 ---------------------------------------------------------------- */

static void uart_init(uint32_t sysclk)
{
    uint32_t div64;

    SYSCTL_RCGC1 |= RCGC1_UART0;
    SYSCTL_RCGC2 |= RCGC2_GPIOA;
    (void)SYSCTL_RCGC2;                 /* a few clocks before the modules are touched */

    GPIO_AFSEL(GPIOA_BASE) |= 0x03;     /* PA0 U0RX, PA1 U0TX */
    GPIO_DEN(GPIOA_BASE) |= 0x03;

    /* divisor = sysclk / (16 * 115200) in 1/64 steps, rounded */
    div64 = (sysclk * 4u + 57600u) / 115200u;
    UART0_CTL = 0;
    UART0_IBRD = div64 >> 6;
    UART0_FBRD = div64 & 0x3Fu;
    UART0_LCRH = 0x70;                  /* 8 data bits, no parity, 1 stop bit, FIFOs on */
    UART0_CTL = 0x301;                  /* UARTEN, TXE, RXE */
}

static void uart_putc(char c)
{
    while (UART0_FR & UART_FR_TXFF)
        ;
    UART0_DR = (uint8_t)c;
}

static void uart_puts(const char *s)
{
    while (*s)
        uart_putc(*s++);
}

static void uart_putu(uint32_t v)
{
    char buf[11];
    int n = 0;

    do {
        buf[n++] = (char)('0' + v % 10u);
        v /= 10u;
    } while (v);
    while (n)
        uart_putc(buf[--n]);
}

static char uart_getc(void)
{
    while (UART0_FR & UART_FR_RXFE)
        ;
    return (char)(UART0_DR & 0xFFu);
}

/* ---- SSI0 ----------------------------------------------------------------- */

static void ssi_init(uint32_t sysclk)
{
    SYSCTL_RCGC1 |= RCGC1_SSI0;
    SYSCTL_RCGC2 |= RCGC2_GPIOA | RCGC2_GPIOD;
    (void)SYSCTL_RCGC2;

    /* SSI0 on PA2 (clock), PA3 (frame), PA4 (rx) and PA5 (tx) */
    GPIO_AFSEL(GPIOA_BASE) |= 0x3C;
    GPIO_DEN(GPIOA_BASE) |= 0x3C;

    /* PD0 drives the card select; idle high */
    GPIO_DIR(GPIOD_BASE) |= SD_CS;
    GPIO_DEN(GPIOD_BASE) |= SD_CS;
    GPIO_DATA(GPIOD_BASE, SD_CS) = SD_CS;

    /* master, Freescale SPI mode 0, 8-bit frames, 400 kHz for card identification */
    SSI0_CR1 = 0;
    SSI0_CPSR = sysclk / 400000u;
    SSI0_CR0 = 0x0007;
    SSI0_CR1 = SSI_CR1_SSE;
}

/* Raise the bit rate once the card has left the identification phase. */
static void ssi_fast(uint32_t sysclk)
{
    (void)sysclk;
    SSI0_CPSR = 2;                      /* half the system clock */
}

static uint8_t spi(uint8_t out)
{
    while (!(SSI0_SR & SSI_SR_TNF))
        ;
    SSI0_DR = out;
    while (!(SSI0_SR & SSI_SR_RNE))
        ;
    return (uint8_t)SSI0_DR;
}

/* ---- SD card in SPI mode -------------------------------------------------- */

static void card_select(void)
{
    GPIO_DATA(GPIOD_BASE, SD_CS) = 0;
    spi(0xFF);
}

static void card_deselect(void)
{
    GPIO_DATA(GPIOD_BASE, SD_CS) = SD_CS;
    spi(0xFF);                          /* lets the card release its data out line */
}

/* Send a command frame and return R1, or 0xFF if the card does not answer. */
static uint8_t sd_command(uint8_t cmd, uint32_t arg, uint8_t crc)
{
    uint8_t r1;
    int n;

    for (n = 0; n < 1000; n++)                          /* >= 8 clocks since the last response, card not busy */
        if (spi(0xFF) == 0xFF)
            break;
    spi((uint8_t)(0x40u | cmd));
    spi((uint8_t)(arg >> 24));
    spi((uint8_t)(arg >> 16));
    spi((uint8_t)(arg >> 8));
    spi((uint8_t)arg);
    spi(crc);
    for (n = 0; n < 10; n++) {
        r1 = spi(0xFF);
        if (!(r1 & 0x80u))
            return r1;
    }
    return 0xFF;
}

static int sd_init(uint32_t sysclk)
{
    uint8_t r1 = 0xFF, r7[4];
    int n;

    /* at least 74 clocks with the card deselected */
    GPIO_DATA(GPIOD_BASE, SD_CS) = SD_CS;
    for (n = 0; n < 10; n++)
        spi(0xFF);

    card_select();
    if (sd_command(0, 0, 0x95) != 0x01) {               /* GO_IDLE_STATE */
        card_deselect();
        return -1;
    }
    if (sd_command(8, 0x000001AAu, 0x87) != 0x01) {     /* SEND_IF_COND */
        card_deselect();
        return -2;
    }
    for (n = 0; n < 4; n++)
        r7[n] = spi(0xFF);
    if (r7[3] != 0xAA) {
        card_deselect();
        return -3;
    }
    for (n = 0; n < 1000; n++) {                        /* SD_SEND_OP_COND until ready */
        sd_command(55, 0, 0x01);
        r1 = sd_command(41, 0x40000000u, 0x01);
        if (r1 == 0x00)
            break;
    }
    if (r1 != 0x00) {
        card_deselect();
        return -4;
    }
    r1 = sd_command(16, 512, 0x01);                     /* SET_BLOCKLEN */
    card_deselect();
    if (r1 != 0x00)
        return -5;

    ssi_fast(sysclk);
    return CARD_SDSC;
}

static int sd_read(uint32_t lba, uint8_t *buf)
{
    uint8_t tok = 0xFF;
    int n;

    card_select();
    if (sd_command(17, lba * 512u, 0x01) != 0x00) {     /* READ_SINGLE_BLOCK */
        card_deselect();
        return -1;
    }
    for (n = 0; n < 10000 && tok == 0xFF; n++)
        tok = spi(0xFF);
    if (tok != 0xFE) {
        card_deselect();
        return -2;
    }
    for (n = 0; n < 512; n++)
        buf[n] = spi(0xFF);
    spi(0xFF);                                          /* CRC, not checked */
    spi(0xFF);
    card_deselect();
    return 0;
}

static int sd_write(uint32_t lba, const uint8_t *buf)
{
    uint8_t resp;
    int n;

    card_select();
    if (sd_command(24, lba * 512u, 0x01) != 0x00) {     /* WRITE_BLOCK */
        card_deselect();
        return -1;
    }
    spi(0xFF);
    spi(0xFE);                                          /* start block token */
    for (n = 0; n < 512; n++)
        spi(buf[n]);
    spi(0xFF);                                          /* CRC, not checked by the card */
    spi(0xFF);
    resp = spi(0xFF);
    if ((resp & 0x1Fu) != 0x05) {                       /* data accepted */
        card_deselect();
        return -2;
    }
    for (n = 0; n < 100000; n++)                        /* busy while programming */
        if (spi(0xFF) == 0xFF)
            break;
    card_deselect();
    return 0;
}

/* ---- host protocol -------------------------------------------------------- */

static char line[1100];
static uint8_t block[512];

static int read_line(void)
{
    int n = 0;
    char c;

    for (;;) {
        c = uart_getc();
        if (c == '\r')
            continue;
        if (c == '\n')
            break;
        if (n < (int)sizeof(line) - 1)
            line[n++] = c;
    }
    line[n] = 0;
    return n;
}

static int hexval(char c)
{
    if (c >= '0' && c <= '9')
        return c - '0';
    if (c >= 'a' && c <= 'f')
        return c - 'a' + 10;
    if (c >= 'A' && c <= 'F')
        return c - 'A' + 10;
    return -1;
}

/* Parse a decimal number at *p; returns 0 on success and advances *p. */
static int parse_u32(const char **p, uint32_t *out)
{
    const char *s = *p;
    uint32_t v = 0;

    while (*s == ' ')
        s++;
    if (*s < '0' || *s > '9')
        return -1;
    while (*s >= '0' && *s <= '9') {
        if (v > 429496729u || (v == 429496729u && *s > '5'))
            return -1;
        v = v * 10u + (uint32_t)(*s++ - '0');
    }
    *p = s;
    *out = v;
    return 0;
}

static void reply_err(int code)
{
    uart_puts("ERR ");
    uart_putu((uint32_t)(code < 0 ? -code : code));
    uart_putc('\n');
}

static void cmd_read(const char *p)
{
    static const char hex[] = "0123456789abcdef";
    uint32_t lba;
    int n, r;

    if (parse_u32(&p, &lba) || *p) {
        reply_err(0);
        return;
    }
    if (card == CARD_NONE) {
        reply_err(9);
        return;
    }
    r = sd_read(lba, block);
    if (r) {
        reply_err(r);
        return;
    }
    uart_puts("DATA ");
    for (n = 0; n < 512; n++) {
        uart_putc(hex[block[n] >> 4]);
        uart_putc(hex[block[n] & 0x0F]);
    }
    uart_putc('\n');
}

static void cmd_write(const char *p)
{
    uint32_t lba;
    int n, hi, lo, r;

    if (parse_u32(&p, &lba) || *p++ != ' ') {
        reply_err(0);
        return;
    }
    for (n = 0; n < 512; n++) {
        hi = hexval(p[2 * n]);
        lo = hi < 0 ? -1 : hexval(p[2 * n + 1]);
        if (lo < 0) {
            reply_err(0);
            return;
        }
        block[n] = (uint8_t)(hi << 4 | lo);
    }
    if (p[1024]) {
        reply_err(0);
        return;
    }
    if (card == CARD_NONE) {
        reply_err(9);
        return;
    }
    r = sd_write(lba, block);
    if (r) {
        reply_err(r);
        return;
    }
    uart_puts("OK\n");
}

void app_main(void)
{
    uint32_t sysclk = clock_init();
    int r;

    uart_init(sysclk);
    ssi_init(sysclk);
    uart_puts("READY\n");

    for (;;) {
        read_line();
        if (line[0] == 'I' && line[1] == 0) {
            card = CARD_NONE;
            r = sd_init(sysclk);
            if (r < 0) {
                reply_err(r);
            } else {
                card = r;
                uart_puts("OK ");
                uart_puts(card_name[card]);
                uart_putc('\n');
            }
        } else if (line[0] == 'R' && line[1] == ' ') {
            cmd_read(line + 1);
        } else if (line[0] == 'W' && line[1] == ' ') {
            cmd_write(line + 1);
        } else {
            reply_err(0);
        }
    }
}
#!/bin/sh
# sh run-sd.sh firmware.elf card.img [v1]
# The board with a microSD card in the slot, UART0 on stdin/stdout (as run.sh).
# The image size must be a power of two: up to 2 GiB is a standard-capacity
# card (SDSC), larger is high capacity (SDHC). Sparse files are fine:
#   truncate -s 64M sdsc.img; truncate -s 4G sdhc.img
# A third argument "v1" makes the card an SD version 1.x card.
#
# QEMU resets RCC to 0x078E3AC0, the silicon to 0x078E3AD1 (datasheet, RCC
# register). The CPU starts in a 24-byte shim at 0x2000FF00 that writes the
# documented value and jumps to the reset vector:
#   ldr r0,=0x400FE060; ldr r1,=0x078E3AD1; str r1,[r0]; movs r0,#4; ldr r0,[r0]; bx r0
elf=$1
img=$2
ver=
[ "${3:-}" = v1 ] && ver="-global sd-card.spec_version=1"
shim=${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/lm3s6965-rcc-shim.bin
printf '\003\110\004\111\001\140\004\040\000\150\000\107\000\277\000\277\140\340\017\100\321\072\216\007' \
    > "$shim.$$" && mv "$shim.$$" "$shim"
exec qemu-system-arm -M lm3s6965evb -nographic -monitor none \
    -chardev stdio,id=uart,mux=off,signal=off -serial chardev:uart \
    -device loader,file="$shim",addr=0x2000FF00,force-raw=on \
    -device loader,addr=0x2000FF01,cpu-num=0 \
    -drive if=sd,format=raw,file="$img" $ver -kernel "$elf"
#!/bin/sh
# sh run.sh firmware.elf: the board, with its UART on stdin/stdout. mux=off so
# that a 0x01 byte on the wire is data and not a QEMU escape.
exec qemu-system-arm -M lm3s6965evb -nographic -monitor none \
    -chardev stdio,id=uart,mux=off,signal=off -serial chardev:uart -kernel "$1"

1066-

1068-
1069-Description:                Following a power-on reset, the JTAG pins TRST, TCK, TMS, TDI, and TDO (PB7 and
1070-                            PC[3:0]) do not have internal pull-ups enabled. Consequently, if these pins are not driven
1071-                            from the board, two things may happen:
1072-                            • The JTAG port may be held in reset and communication with a four-pin JTAG-based
1073-                                debugger may be intermittent or impossible.
1074-                            • The receivers may draw excess current.
1075-
1076-Workaround(s):              There are a number of workarounds for this problem, varying in complexity and impact:
1077-                            1. Add external pull-up resistors to all of the affected pins. This workaround solves both
1078-                               issues of JTAG connectivity and current consumption.
1079-                            2. Add an external pull-up resistor to TRST. Firmware should enable the internal pull-
1080-                               ups on the affected pins by setting the appropriate PUE bits of the appropriate GPIO
1081-                               Pull-Up Select (GPIOPUR) registers as early in the reset handler as possible. This
1082-                               workaround addresses the issue of JTAG connectivity, but does not address the
1083-                               current consumption other than to limit the affected period (from power-on reset to
1084-                               code execution).
1085-                            3. Pull-ups on the JTAG pins are unnecessary for code loaded via the SWD interface or
1086-                               via the serial boot loader. Loaded firmware should enable the internal pull-ups on the
1087-                               affected pins by setting the appropriate PUE bits of the appropriate GPIOPUR

Other Peripherals
Speaker
           A small, magnetic audio transducer connects through a MOSFET to PD1/PWM1, allowing a range
           of options for generating simple and complex tones. Use of the +5-V rail reduces switching noise
           on the +3.3-V rail.

MicroSD Card Slot
           Removable Flash cards are an ideal media for storing data such as web page content. The source
           code on the CD includes example code for reading data from standard FAT formatted SD cards.
           All data and control transactions use the SD card’s SPI mode. Note that the SD card specification
           does not require that a card supports the SPI mode, but most cards do so in practice. Cards from
           several vendors have been used with the EVB.
           MicroSD cards are very small and require careful handling. the SD card slot on the EVB is a push-
           push type (push to insert; push again to eject).
           Note: To avoid damage, remove power before inserting or removing cards.The EVB does not
           implement SD card power control.

Push Switches
           The EVB has five general-purpose input switches. Four are arranged in a navigation-style
           configuration. The fifth functions as a Select switch.

User LED
            A user LED (LED3) is provided for general use. The LED is connected to PC5/CCP1, allowing the

Bypassing Peripherals
            Excluding Ethernet, the EVB’s on-board peripheral circuits require 16 GPIO lines. Two additional
            GPIO lines are assigned to Ethernet LEDs. This leaves 20 GPIO lines and 4 ADC channels
            immediately available for connection to external circuits. If an application requires more GPIO
            lines, the on-board hardware can be disconnected. The EVB is populated with 16 jumper links,
            which can be cut with a knife to isolate on-board hardware. The process can be reversed by
            installing 0603- 0-ohm chip resistors.
            Important: The quickstart application will not run if one or more jumpers are removed.
