cat > /app/firmware.c <<'EOF'
/*
 * microSD block service for the EK-LM3S6965 evaluation board.
 *
 * The host drives the card through UART0 (virtual COM port, 115200 8N1).
 * One command per line ('\n'), answered with one line:
 *
 *   I                    initialise the card  -> "OK SDSC", "OK SDHC", "OK SDV1" or "ERR <n>"
 *   R <lba>              read block <lba>     -> "DATA <1024 hex digits>" or "ERR <n>"
 *   W <lba> <1024 hex>   write block <lba>    -> "OK" or "ERR <n>"
 *
 * <lba> is a decimal 512-byte block number. "READY" is printed once after
 * reset. A malformed line is answered with "ERR 0".
 *
 * Board details (EK-LM3S6965, LM3S6965 Rev A2 "Fury" silicon):
 *   clock   8 MHz crystal on OSC0/OSC1 -> MOSC -> PLL (400 MHz) / SYSDIV2 -> 50 MHz
 *   UART0   PA0 U0RX, PA1 U0TX, 115200 8N1
 *   SSI0    PA2 CLK, PA3 FSS, PA4 RX (card DO), PA5 TX (card DI); PD0 = card CS
 *   OLED    shares SSI0 CLK/TX: PA3 FSS = OLED CS, PC7 = OLED D/C.  The OLED
 *           controller cannot be read back, so it is held in reset with its
 *           chip select inactive - otherwise every card transaction clocks
 *           SPI data into the display and shows up as random pixels.
 */
#include <stdint.h>

#define REG(a)          (*(volatile uint32_t *)(a))

/* System control */
#define SYSCTL_DID0     REG(0x400FE000)
#define SYSCTL_LDOPCTL  REG(0x400FE034)
#define SYSCTL_RIS      REG(0x400FE050)
#define SYSCTL_RCC      REG(0x400FE060)
#define SYSCTL_PLLCFG   REG(0x400FE064)
#define SYSCTL_RCC2     REG(0x400FE070)
#define SYSCTL_RCGC1    REG(0x400FE104)
#define SYSCTL_RCGC2    REG(0x400FE108)

#define RCGC1_UART0     0x00000001u
#define RCGC1_SSI0      0x00000010u
#define RCGC2_GPIOA     0x00000001u
#define RCGC2_GPIOC     0x00000004u
#define RCGC2_GPIOD     0x00000008u

/* RCC */
#define RCC_MOSCDIS     0x00000001u     /* 1 = main oscillator disabled */
#define RCC_IOSCDIS     0x00000002u     /* 1 = internal oscillator disabled */
#define RCC_OSCSRC_M    0x00000030u     /* oscillator source */
#define RCC_OSCSRC_MOSC 0x00000000u
#define RCC_OSCSRC_IOSC 0x00000010u
#define RCC_XTAL_M      0x000003C0u     /* crystal value */
#define RCC_XTAL_8MHZ   0x00000380u     /* 0xE */
#define RCC_BYPASS      0x00000800u     /* 1 = do not use the PLL */
#define RCC_PWRDN       0x00002000u     /* 1 = PLL powered down */
#define RCC_USESYSDIV   0x00400000u
#define RCC_SYSDIV_M    0x07800000u
#define RCC_SYSDIV_4    0x01800000u     /* SYSDIV = 3, 200 MHz / 4 = 50 MHz */
#define RCC_ACG         0x08000000u

/* RCC2 */
#define RCC2_OSCSRC2_M    0x00000070u
#define RCC2_OSCSRC2_MOSC 0x00000000u
#define RCC2_OSCSRC2_IOSC 0x00000010u
#define RCC2_BYPASS2      0x00000800u
#define RCC2_PWRDN2       0x00002000u
#define RCC2_SYSDIV2_M    0x1F800000u
#define RCC2_SYSDIV2_4    0x01800000u   /* 200 MHz / (3 + 1) = 50 MHz */
#define RCC2_USERPCLK     0x00000001u
#define RCC2_USERCC2      0x80000000u

#define RIS_PLLLRIS     0x00000040u
#define LDOPCTL_2V75    0x1Bu

/* Clock the firmware runs at: PLL 400 MHz / 2 / 4. */
#define SYSCLK_HZ       50000000u

/* GPIO; the data register is addressed through a bit mask in address bits [9:2] */
#define GPIOA_BASE      0x40004000u
#define GPIOC_BASE      0x40006000u
#define GPIOD_BASE      0x40007000u
#define GPIO_DATA(b, m) REG((b) + ((uint32_t)(m) << 2))
#define GPIO_DIR(b)     REG((b) + 0x400u)
#define GPIO_AFSEL(b)   REG((b) + 0x420u)
#define GPIO_DEN(b)     REG((b) + 0x51Cu)

/* UART0 */
#define UART0_DR        REG(0x4000C000)
#define UART0_FR        REG(0x4000C018)
#define UART0_IBRD      REG(0x4000C024)
#define UART0_FBRD      REG(0x4000C028)
#define UART0_LCRH      REG(0x4000C02C)
#define UART0_CTL       REG(0x4000C030)
#define UART_FR_RXFE    0x10u
#define UART_FR_TXFF    0x20u

/* SSI0 */
#define SSI0_CR0        REG(0x40008000)
#define SSI0_CR1        REG(0x40008004)
#define SSI0_DR         REG(0x40008008)
#define SSI0_SR         REG(0x4000800C)
#define SSI0_CPSR       REG(0x40008010)
#define SSI_CR1_SSE     0x02u
#define SSI_SR_TNF      0x02u
#define SSI_SR_RNE      0x04u
#define SSI_CR0_8BIT    0x0007u         /* Freescale SPI, mode 0, DSS = 8 */

/* PA3 is SSI0FSS: the OLED chip select when the pin is in GPIO mode. */
#define OLED_CS         0x08u
#define OLED_DC         0x80u           /* PC7, OLED data/control select */

#define SD_CS           0x01u           /* PD0, card select, active low */

enum { CARD_NONE = -1, CARD_SDSC, CARD_SDHC, CARD_SDV1 };
static const char *const card_name[] = { "SDSC", "SDHC", "SDV1" };

static int card = CARD_NONE;
static int card_hc = 0;                 /* 1: block addressed (SDHC), 0: byte addressed */
static uint32_t sysclk = SYSCLK_HZ;

/* ---- clock ---------------------------------------------------------------- */

/*
 * 50 MHz from the 8 MHz crystal through the PLL.  The board carries LM3S6965
 * Rev A2 (Fury) silicon, so two errata apply:
 *
 * LM3SYSCTL#09  the PLL is unstable with the LDO at its default 2.5 V, so the
 *               LDO is set to 2.75 V before the PLL is powered up.  This is
 *               what made two units lock up at 50 MHz.
 * LM3SYSCTL#11  an external reset leaves XTAL at 6 MHz but PLLCFG at whatever
 *               was programmed before; PLLCFG is only updated on a *change* of
 *               XTAL, so it is first written with a different crystal value
 *               and then with the real one.
 *
 * The main oscillator is given time to start before it is selected, and the
 * PLL lock flag (RIS.PLLLRIS, ~0.5 ms) is waited for before the bypass is
 * removed.  That is what fixed the units whose console was garbled from
 * power-up.
 */
static void clock_init(void)
{
    uint32_t rcc, rcc2, v;
    int n;

    /* LM3SYSCTL#09: run the LDO at 2.75 V before the PLL is enabled. */
    v = SYSCTL_LDOPCTL;
    if ((v & 0x3Fu) != LDOPCTL_2V75)
        SYSCTL_LDOPCTL = (v & ~0x3Fu) | LDOPCTL_2V75;
    for (n = 0; n < 16; n++)
        (void)SYSCTL_LDOPCTL;

    /* Start from the documented reset values, not from whatever is there. */
    rcc  = 0x078E3AD1u;
    rcc2 = 0x07802810u;

    /* 1. Bypass the PLL and the system clock divider, run off the internal
     *    oscillator.  MOSCDIS is cleared so the main oscillator starts. */
    rcc  = (rcc  & ~(RCC_SYSDIV_M | RCC_USESYSDIV | RCC_BYPASS | RCC_PWRDN |
                     RCC_OSCSRC_M | RCC_XTAL_M | RCC_ACG))
         | RCC_BYPASS | RCC_PWRDN | RCC_OSCSRC_IOSC | 0x3C0u;   /* XTAL = 0xF */
    rcc2 = (rcc2 & ~(RCC2_SYSDIV2_M | RCC2_BYPASS2 | RCC2_PWRDN2 |
                     RCC2_OSCSRC2_M | RCC2_USERPCLK))
         | RCC2_BYPASS2 | RCC2_PWRDN2 | RCC2_OSCSRC2_IOSC;
    SYSCTL_RCC  = rcc;
    SYSCTL_RCC2 = rcc2;

    /* 2. LM3SYSCTL#11: force a change of XTAL so PLLCFG is re-translated.
     *    An invalid value first, then the 8 MHz crystal that is fitted. */
    rcc = (rcc & ~RCC_XTAL_M) | 0x3C0u;                         /* XTAL = 0xF */
    SYSCTL_RCC = rcc;
    rcc = (rcc & ~RCC_XTAL_M) | RCC_XTAL_8MHZ;                  /* XTAL = 0xE */
    SYSCTL_RCC = rcc;
    for (n = 0; n < 16; n++)
        (void)SYSCTL_RCC;

    /* Let the main oscillator start and settle before it is selected. */
    for (n = 0; n < 20000; n++)
        (void)SYSCTL_RCC;

    /* 3. Use the main oscillator as the PLL reference and power the PLL up. */
    rcc  = (rcc  & ~RCC_OSCSRC_M) | RCC_OSCSRC_MOSC;
    rcc2 = (rcc2 & ~RCC2_OSCSRC2_M) | RCC2_OSCSRC2_MOSC | RCC2_USERCC2;
    SYSCTL_RCC  = rcc;
    SYSCTL_RCC2 = rcc2;

    rcc  &= ~RCC_PWRDN;
    rcc2 &= ~RCC2_PWRDN2;
    SYSCTL_RCC  = rcc;
    SYSCTL_RCC2 = rcc2;

    /* 4. Set the divider for 50 MHz: 400 MHz / 2 / (3 + 1). */
    rcc  = (rcc  & ~RCC_SYSDIV_M) | RCC_SYSDIV_4;
    rcc2 = (rcc2 & ~RCC2_SYSDIV2_M) | RCC2_SYSDIV2_4;
    SYSCTL_RCC  = rcc;
    SYSCTL_RCC2 = rcc2;

    /* 5. Wait for the PLL to lock (TREADY = 0.5 ms maximum). */
    for (n = 0; n < 2000000 && !(SYSCTL_RIS & RIS_PLLLRIS); n++)
        (void)SYSCTL_RIS;

    /* 6. Clear the bypass: the system now runs from the PLL. */
    rcc  &= ~RCC_BYPASS;
    rcc2 &= ~RCC2_BYPASS2;
    SYSCTL_RCC  = rcc;
    SYSCTL_RCC2 = rcc2;

    /* A few system clocks before anything uses the new rate. */
    for (n = 0; n < 64; n++)
        (void)SYSCTL_RCC;

    sysclk = SYSCLK_HZ;
}

/* ---- UART0 ---------------------------------------------------------------- */

static void uart_init(uint32_t clk)
{
    uint32_t div64;

    SYSCTL_RCGC1 |= RCGC1_UART0;
    SYSCTL_RCGC2 |= RCGC2_GPIOA;
    (void)SYSCTL_RCGC2;                 /* a few clocks before the modules are touched */
    (void)SYSCTL_RCGC2;

    GPIO_AFSEL(GPIOA_BASE) |= 0x03;     /* PA0 U0RX, PA1 U0TX */
    GPIO_DEN(GPIOA_BASE) |= 0x03;

    /* divisor = clk / (16 * 115200) in 1/64 steps, rounded */
    div64 = (clk * 4u + 57600u) / 115200u;
    UART0_CTL = 0;
    UART0_IBRD = div64 >> 6;
    UART0_FBRD = div64 & 0x3Fu;
    UART0_LCRH = 0x70;                  /* 8 data bits, no parity, 1 stop bit, FIFOs on */
    UART0_CTL = 0x301;                  /* UARTEN, TXE, RXE */
}

static void uart_putc(char c)
{
    while (UART0_FR & UART_FR_TXFF)
        ;
    UART0_DR = (uint8_t)c;
}

static void uart_puts(const char *s)
{
    while (*s)
        uart_putc(*s++);
}

static void uart_putu(uint32_t v)
{
    char buf[11];
    int n = 0;

    do {
        buf[n++] = (char)('0' + v % 10u);
        v /= 10u;
    } while (v);
    while (n)
        uart_putc(buf[--n]);
}

static char uart_getc(void)
{
    while (UART0_FR & UART_FR_RXFE)
        ;
    return (char)(UART0_DR & 0xFFu);
}

/* ---- SSI0 ----------------------------------------------------------------- */

/* SSIClk = SysClk / (CPSDVSR * (1 + SCR)); CPSDVSR is even, 2..254. */
static void ssi_rate(uint32_t hz)
{
    uint32_t prescale, scr;

    prescale = sysclk / hz;
    if (prescale < 2u)
        prescale = 2u;
    prescale &= ~1u;                    /* must be even */
    if (prescale > 254u)
        prescale = 254u;

    scr = sysclk / (prescale * hz);
    if (scr)
        scr--;
    if (scr > 255u)
        scr = 255u;

    SSI0_CR1 = 0;                       /* disabled while CR0 is written */
    SSI0_CPSR = prescale;
    SSI0_CR0 = SSI_CR0_8BIT | (scr << 8);
    SSI0_CR1 = SSI_CR1_SSE;
}

static void ssi_init(uint32_t clk)
{
    (void)clk;

    SYSCTL_RCGC1 |= RCGC1_SSI0;
    SYSCTL_RCGC2 |= RCGC2_GPIOA | RCGC2_GPIOC | RCGC2_GPIOD;
    (void)SYSCTL_RCGC2;
    (void)SYSCTL_RCGC2;

    /* Keep the OLED out of the way before the SSI pins are turned on: it sits
     * on the same clock and data-in lines and its controller cannot be read
     * back, so any traffic it sees is displayed as random pixels.  PA3 doubles
     * as its chip select, so it is driven high as a plain output first. */
    GPIO_DATA(GPIOA_BASE, OLED_CS) = OLED_CS;
    GPIO_DIR(GPIOA_BASE) |= OLED_CS;
    GPIO_AFSEL(GPIOA_BASE) &= ~OLED_CS;
    GPIO_DEN(GPIOA_BASE) |= OLED_CS;

    GPIO_DATA(GPIOC_BASE, OLED_DC) = OLED_DC;
    GPIO_DIR(GPIOC_BASE) |= OLED_DC;
    GPIO_AFSEL(GPIOC_BASE) &= ~OLED_DC;
    GPIO_DEN(GPIOC_BASE) |= OLED_DC;

    /* SSI0 on PA2 (clock), PA4 (rx) and PA5 (tx); PA3 stays the OLED CS. */
    GPIO_AFSEL(GPIOA_BASE) |= 0x34u;
    GPIO_DEN(GPIOA_BASE) |= 0x34u;

    /* PD0 drives the card select; idle high. */
    GPIO_DATA(GPIOD_BASE, SD_CS) = SD_CS;
    GPIO_DIR(GPIOD_BASE) |= SD_CS;
    GPIO_AFSEL(GPIOD_BASE) &= ~SD_CS;
    GPIO_DEN(GPIOD_BASE) |= SD_CS;

    /* Card identification runs at 100-400 kHz. */
    SSI0_CR1 = 0;
    ssi_rate(200000u);
}

/* Raise the bit rate once the card has left the identification phase. */
static void ssi_fast(uint32_t clk)
{
    (void)clk;
    ssi_rate(12500000u);                /* SysClk / 4 */
}

static uint8_t spi(uint8_t out)
{
    while (!(SSI0_SR & SSI_SR_TNF))
        ;
    SSI0_DR = out;
    while (!(SSI0_SR & SSI_SR_RNE))
        ;
    return (uint8_t)SSI0_DR;
}

/* ---- SD card in SPI mode -------------------------------------------------- */

static void card_select(void)
{
    GPIO_DATA(GPIOD_BASE, SD_CS) = 0;
}

static void card_deselect(void)
{
    GPIO_DATA(GPIOD_BASE, SD_CS) = SD_CS;
    spi(0xFF);                          /* lets the card release its data out line */
}

/* Wait until the card is not busy; returns 0 on success. */
static int card_wait_busy(uint32_t limit)
{
    uint32_t n;

    for (n = 0; n < limit; n++)
        if (spi(0xFF) == 0xFF)
            return 0;
    return -1;
}

/* Send a command frame and return R1, or 0xFF if the card does not answer.
 * The caller must have selected the card. */
static uint8_t sd_command(uint8_t cmd, uint32_t arg, uint8_t crc)
{
    uint8_t r1;
    int n;

    spi((uint8_t)(0x40u | cmd));
    spi((uint8_t)(arg >> 24));
    spi((uint8_t)(arg >> 16));
    spi((uint8_t)(arg >> 8));
    spi((uint8_t)arg);
    spi(crc);
    for (n = 0; n < 10; n++) {
        r1 = spi(0xFF);
        if (!(r1 & 0x80u))
            return r1;
    }
    return 0xFF;
}

/* Read the 4-byte payload of an R7 response. */
static void sd_read_r7(uint8_t *r7)
{
    int n;

    for (n = 0; n < 4; n++)
        r7[n] = spi(0xFF);
}

static int sd_init(uint32_t clk)
{
    uint8_t r1 = 0xFF, r7[4], ocr[4];
    uint32_t n;
    int v2, hc, i;

    (void)clk;

    /* Always start from the identification rate; the card may already be
     * initialised from an earlier run. */
    ssi_rate(200000u);
    card_hc = 0;

    /* at least 74 clocks with the card deselected */
    GPIO_DATA(GPIOD_BASE, SD_CS) = SD_CS;
    for (n = 0; n < 16; n++)
        spi(0xFF);

    card_select();
    if (sd_command(0, 0, 0x95) != 0x01) {               /* GO_IDLE_STATE, SPI mode */
        card_deselect();
        return -1;
    }
    card_deselect();

    /* SEND_IF_COND tells version 2.00 cards from version 1.x cards.  A
     * version 1.x card answers with the illegal-command bit set. */
    card_select();
    r1 = sd_command(8, 0x000001AAu, 0x87);
    if (!(r1 & 0x04u) && r1 != 0xFF)
        sd_read_r7(r7);
    card_deselect();
    v2 = (r1 == 0x01);
    if (v2 && r7[2] != 0x01) {                          /* voltage range not 2.7-3.6 V */
        if (r7[3] != 0xAA)
            return -3;
    }
    if (v2 && r7[3] != 0xAA)
        return -3;

    /* ACMD41 until the card leaves the idle state.  HCS is only understood by
     * version 2.00 cards.  The first attempt uses the CRC that is right for
     * the card type in hand, so a version 1.x card is not rejected while it
     * is still checking command CRCs. */
    hc = 0;
    for (i = 0; i < 2; i++) {
        for (n = 0; n < 100000; n++) {
            card_select();
            sd_command(55, 0, 0x01);                    /* APP_CMD */
            card_deselect();
            card_select();
            r1 = sd_command(41, v2 ? 0x40000000u : 0u, v2 ? 0x77u : 0xE5u);
            card_deselect();
            if (r1 == 0x00)
                break;
            if (r1 == 0xFF || (r1 & 0x0Cu))             /* no answer or command error */
                break;
            /* wait, the card can need hundreds of milliseconds */
            { uint32_t d; for (d = 0; d < 20000; d++) (void)d; }
        }
        if (r1 == 0x00)
            break;
        if (i == 0 && v2) {                             /* retry without HCS */
            v2 = 0;
            continue;
        }
        return -4;
    }
    if (r1 != 0x00)
        return -4;

    /* A version 2.00 card reports its capacity in the OCR. */
    if (v2) {
        card_select();
        if (sd_command(58, 0, 0xFD) != 0x00) {          /* READ_OCR */
            card_deselect();
            return -5;
        }
        sd_read_r7(ocr);
        card_deselect();
        hc = (ocr[0] & 0x40u) != 0;                     /* CCS: card is block addressed */
    }

    card_select();
    r1 = sd_command(16, 512, 0x01);                     /* SET_BLOCKLEN, needed by SDSC */
    card_deselect();
    if (r1 != 0x00)
        return -6;

    if (card_wait_busy(1000000u)) {
        card_deselect();
        return -7;
    }
    card_deselect();

    ssi_fast(sysclk);

    card_hc = hc;
    if (hc)
        return CARD_SDHC;
    return v2 ? CARD_SDSC : CARD_SDV1;
}

/* Address a block: SDHC cards take a block number, SDSC and version 1.x
 * cards take a byte address. */
static uint32_t sd_addr(uint32_t lba)
{
    if (card_hc)
        return lba;
    return lba * 512u;                                  /* 512u keeps the 32-bit product */
}

static int sd_read(uint32_t lba, uint8_t *buf)
{
    uint8_t tok = 0xFF;
    int n;

    card_select();
    if (sd_command(17, sd_addr(lba), 0x01) != 0x00) {   /* READ_SINGLE_BLOCK */
        card_deselect();
        return -1;
    }
    for (n = 0; n < 100000 && tok == 0xFF; n++)
        tok = spi(0xFF);
    if (tok != 0xFE) {
        card_deselect();
        return -2;
    }
    for (n = 0; n < 512; n++)
        buf[n] = spi(0xFF);
    spi(0xFF);                                          /* CRC, not checked */
    spi(0xFF);
    card_deselect();
    return 0;
}

static int sd_write(uint32_t lba, const uint8_t *buf)
{
    uint8_t resp;
    int n;

    card_select();
    if (sd_command(24, sd_addr(lba), 0x01) != 0x00) {   /* WRITE_BLOCK */
        card_deselect();
        return -1;
    }
    spi(0xFF);
    spi(0xFE);                                          /* start block token */
    for (n = 0; n < 512; n++)
        spi(buf[n]);
    spi(0xFF);                                          /* CRC, not checked by the card */
    spi(0xFF);
    resp = spi(0xFF);
    if ((resp & 0x1Fu) != 0x05) {                       /* data accepted */
        card_deselect();
        return -2;
    }
    if (card_wait_busy(5000000u)) {                     /* busy while programming */
        card_deselect();
        return -3;
    }
    card_deselect();
    return 0;
}

/* ---- host protocol -------------------------------------------------------- */

static char line[1100];
static uint8_t block[512];

static int read_line(void)
{
    int n = 0;
    char c;

    for (;;) {
        c = uart_getc();
        if (c == '\r')
            continue;
        if (c == '\n')
            break;
        if (n < (int)sizeof(line) - 1)
            line[n++] = c;
    }
    line[n] = 0;
    return n;
}

static int hexval(char c)
{
    if (c >= '0' && c <= '9')
        return c - '0';
    if (c >= 'a' && c <= 'f')
        return c - 'a' + 10;
    if (c >= 'A' && c <= 'F')
        return c - 'A' + 10;
    return -1;
}

/* Parse a decimal number at *p; returns 0 on success and advances *p. */
static int parse_u32(const char **p, uint32_t *out)
{
    const char *s = *p;
    uint32_t v = 0;

    while (*s == ' ')
        s++;
    if (*s < '0' || *s > '9')
        return -1;
    while (*s >= '0' && *s <= '9') {
        if (v > 429496729u || (v == 429496729u && *s > '5'))
            return -1;
        v = v * 10u + (uint32_t)(*s++ - '0');
    }
    *p = s;
    *out = v;
    return 0;
}

static void reply_err(int code)
{
    uart_puts("ERR ");
    uart_putu((uint32_t)(code < 0 ? -code : code));
    uart_putc('\n');
}

static void cmd_read(const char *p)
{
    static const char hex[] = "0123456789abcdef";
    uint32_t lba;
    int n, r;

    if (parse_u32(&p, &lba) || *p) {
        reply_err(0);
        return;
    }
    if (card == CARD_NONE) {
        reply_err(9);
        return;
    }
    r = sd_read(lba, block);
    if (r) {
        reply_err(r);
        return;
    }
    uart_puts("DATA ");
    for (n = 0; n < 512; n++) {
        uart_putc(hex[block[n] >> 4]);
        uart_putc(hex[block[n] & 0x0F]);
    }
    uart_putc('\n');
}

static void cmd_write(const char *p)
{
    uint32_t lba;
    int n, hi, lo, r;

    if (parse_u32(&p, &lba) || *p++ != ' ') {
        reply_err(0);
        return;
    }
    for (n = 0; n < 512; n++) {
        hi = hexval(p[2 * n]);
        lo = hi < 0 ? -1 : hexval(p[2 * n + 1]);
        if (lo < 0) {
            reply_err(0);
            return;
        }
        block[n] = (uint8_t)(hi << 4 | lo);
    }
    if (p[1024]) {
        reply_err(0);
        return;
    }
    if (card == CARD_NONE) {
        reply_err(9);
        return;
    }
    r = sd_write(lba, block);
    if (r) {
        reply_err(r);
        return;
    }
    uart_puts("OK\n");
}

void app_main(void)
{
    int r;

    clock_init();
    uart_init(sysclk);
    ssi_init(sysclk);
    uart_puts("READY\n");

    for (;;) {
        read_line();
        if (line[0] == 'I' && line[1] == 0) {
            card = CARD_NONE;
            card_hc = 0;
            r = sd_init(sysclk);
            if (r < 0) {
                reply_err(r);
            } else {
                card = r;
                uart_puts("OK ");
                uart_puts(card_name[card]);
                uart_putc('\n');
            }
        } else if (line[0] == 'R' && line[1] == ' ') {
            cmd_read(line + 1);
        } else if (line[0] == 'W' && line[1] == ' ') {
            cmd_write(line + 1);
        } else {
            reply_err(0);
```c
        }
```
```c
    }
```
```c
}
```

```
static uint32_t clock_init(void)
{
    uint32_t rcc, rcc2;
    volatile uint32_t d;

    /* LM3SYSCTL#09: raise the LDO to 2.75 V before the PLL is enabled,
       otherwise the PLL output is unstable (units lock up at 50 MHz). */
    SYSCTL_LDOPCTL = LDOV_2_75;

    /* LM3SYSCTL#25: a brown-out must reset the device. */
    SYSCTL_PBORCTL |= 0x2;

    /* ... MOSC enable ... */
    rcc = RCC_VALUE;               /* bypass, PWRDN, XTAL=8 MHz, OSCSRC=MOSC */
    rcc2 = RCC2_VALUE;
    SYSCTL_RCC = rcc;
    SYSCTL_RCC2 = rcc2;
    for (d = 0; d < 16; d++) (void)SYSCTL_RCC;   /* allow the MOSC to start */

    /* LM3SYSCTL#11: an external reset leaves PLLCFG at the previous XTAL
       value, and a write of the same XTAL value does not update it. Change
       XTAL to another legal value first, then back. */
    SYSCTL_RCC = (rcc & ~RCC_XTAL_M) | (XTAL_5MHZ << 6);
    delay();
    SYSCTL_RCC = rcc;
    delay();

    /* PLL up, still bypassed */
    rcc &= ~RCC_PWRDN;
    rcc2 &= ~RCC2_PWRDN2;
    SYSCTL_RCC = rcc;
    SYSCTL_RCC2 = rcc2;

    /* wait for lock */
    timeout = ...;
    while (!(SYSCTL_RIS & RIS_PLLLRIS) && timeout--) delay(1);

    /* switch to the PLL */
    rcc &= ~RCC_BYPASS;
    rcc2 &= ~RCC2_BYPASS2;
    SYSCTL_RCC = rcc;
    SYSCTL_RCC2 = rcc2;

    return SYSCLK_HZ;
}
```

Bitwise MSB-first implementation with an 8-bit accumulator holding the CRC in bits [7:1]:
```c
uint8_t crc7(const uint8_t *data, int len) {
    uint8_t crc = 0;
    for (int i = 0; i < len; i++) {
        crc ^= data[i];
        for (int j = 0; j < 8; j++) {
            if (crc & 0x80) crc = (crc << 1) ^ 0x12;   /* 0x12 = poly 0x09 << 1 */
            else crc <<= 1;

    return (crc >> 1) | 0x80;   /* 7-bit CRC + stop bit */

```
Hmm, let me verify: The common implementation (from fatfs and many places):

```c

    BYTE crc = 0;
```

The classic bit-serial algorithm (from the SD spec, MSB first, 7-bit LFSR with poly x^7+x^3+1):

```c
static uint8_t crc7(uint8_t crc, uint8_t d) {
    int i;
    for (i = 0; i < 8; i++) {
        uint8_t msb = (crc >> 6) & 1;       /* crc holds 7 bits in [6:0] */
        uint8_t in = (d >> (7 - i)) & 1;
        uint8_t fb = msb ^ in;
        crc = (uint8_t)((crc << 1) & 0x7F);
        if (fb) crc ^= 0x09;
    }
    return crc;
}
```
This is the standard LFSR feedback form: for a 7-bit register with poly x^7+x^3+1 (0x09 = bit0 (x^0) + bit3 (x^3)). Let me verify: the CRC register is c6..c0 (c6 = MSB). Feedback = c6 XOR input_bit. New register: shift left; c0 = feedback*poly_bit0 = fb; c3 ^= fb (x^3 term). So crc = ((crc << 1) & 0x7F) ^ (fb ? 0x09 : 0). Yes, that's what I wrote (0x09 = bits 0 and 3).

Then the transmitted byte = (crc << 1) | 1.

```c
static uint32_t loop_us;   /* delay-loop iterations per microsecond */

static void us_delay(uint32_t us)
{
    volatile uint32_t n = us * loop_us;
    while (n)
        n--;

static void ms_delay(uint32_t ms) { while (ms--) us_delay(1000u); }
```
With volatile, each iteration is a load, subtract, store, compare, branch ≈ 5-6 cycles. So loop_us = sysclk/1e6/6 ≈ 8 for 50 MHz. SSI clock functions:

```c
static uint32_t ssi_hz;   /* current SSI bit rate, for reference */

/* SSI bit rate = FSysClk / (CPSDVSR * (1 + SCR)) */
static void ssi_rate(uint32_t sysclk, uint32_t target_hz)
{
    uint32_t cpsr, scr;
    /* pick the largest even prescaler that keeps the rate at or below the target */
    cpsr = sysclk / target_hz;
    if (cpsr < 2) cpsr = 2;
    if (cpsr > 254) cpsr = 254;
    cpsr &= ~1u;   /* must be even */
    /* hmm: if cpsr becomes 0 after masking... */
    scr = (sysclk / (cpsr * target_hz)) - 1; ...
}
```
Careful with rounding: we want rate <= target. Let me compute: divisor_total = ceil(sysclk / target). Then find even cpsr and scr such that cpsr*(1+scr) >= divisor_total, with cpsr even in [2,254], scr in [0,255].

Simple approach: cpsr = 2; while (sysclk / (cpsr * target) ... hmm.

Simplest correct approach:
```c
static void ssi_rate(uint32_t sysclk, uint32_t target)
{
    uint32_t total = (sysclk + target - 1) / target;   /* smallest divisor giving <= target */
    uint32_t cpsr;
    if (total < 2) total = 2;
    if (total > 254 * 256) total = 254 * 256;
    cpsr = ((total + 1) / 2) * 2;      /* round up to even */
    if (cpsr > 254) cpsr = 254;
    /* scr = ceil(total / cpsr) - 1 */
    uint32_t scr = (total + cpsr - 1) / cpsr;
    if (scr) scr -= 1; else scr = 0;
    if (scr > 255) { scr = 255; }   /* can't happen given total clamp */
    SSI0_CR1 = 0;               /* disable while reconfiguring */
    SSI0_CPSR = cpsr;
    SSI0_CR0 = (SSI0_CR0 & 0xFF00u) | ((scr << 8) & 0xFF00u) | ...
```
Hmm, CR0 also holds FRF/SPO/SPH/DSS in bits 7:0, and SCR in 15:8. Since we always configure CR0 fully elsewhere, let me store a static `cr0_base = 0x07` (SPI mode 0, 8-bit) and write `SSI0_CR0 = cr0_base | (scr << 8)`.

For identification: target 400 kHz (spec allows 100–400 kHz; I'll use 400 kHz, the top of the identification range → sysclk/400000 = 125 → cpsr=126 (even, ceil) → rate = 50e6/126 = 396.8 kHz ✓ within [100,400] kHz.

#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdint.h>
static uint8_t crc7(uint8_t crc, uint8_t d)
{
    int i;
    for (i = 0; i < 8; i++) {
        uint8_t fb = (uint8_t)(((crc >> 6) ^ (d >> 7)) & 1u);
        crc = (uint8_t)((crc << 1) & 0x7Fu);
        d = (uint8_t)(d << 1);
        if (fb) crc ^= 0x09u;
    }
    return crc;
}
static uint8_t cmdcrc(uint8_t cmd, uint32_t arg)
{
    uint8_t b[5]; uint8_t c = 0; int i;
    b[0] = (uint8_t)(0x40u | cmd);
    b[1] = (uint8_t)(arg >> 24); b[2] = (uint8_t)(arg >> 16);
    b[3] = (uint8_t)(arg >> 8);  b[4] = (uint8_t)arg;
    for (i = 0; i < 5; i++) c = crc7(c, b[i]);
    return (uint8_t)((c << 1) | 1u);
}
int main(void)
{
    printf("CMD0   = 0x%02X (want 0x95)\n", cmdcrc(0, 0));
    printf("CMD8   = 0x%02X (want 0x87)\n", cmdcrc(8, 0x1AA));
    printf("CMD16  = 0x%02X\n", cmdcrc(16, 512));
    printf("CMD17  = 0x%02X\n", cmdcrc(17, 1024));
    printf("CMD55  = 0x%02X\n", cmdcrc(55, 0));
    printf("CMD41  = 0x%02X\n", cmdcrc(41, 0x40000000u));
    printf("CMD58  = 0x%02X\n", cmdcrc(58, 0));
    printf("CMD59  = 0x%02X\n", cmdcrc(59, 0));
    /* RCC values */
    unsigned rcc = (1u<<27)|(0xFu<<23)|(1u<<22)|(1u<<20)|(7u<<17)|(1u<<13)|(1u<<11)|(0xEu<<6)|(0u<<4)|(0u<<1);
    unsigned rcc2 = (1u<<31)|(3u<<23)|(1u<<13)|(1u<<11)|(0u<<4);
    printf("RCC=0x%08X RCC2=0x%08X\n", rcc, rcc2);
    printf("50MHz uart div64 = %u -> IBRD=%u FBRD=%u (baud=%.1f)\n",
        (50000000u*4u + 57600u)/115200u, ((50000000u*4u+57600u)/115200u)>>6, ((50000000u*4u+57600u)/115200u)&0x3F,
        50000000.0/(16.0*(((50000000u*4u+57600u)/115200u)/64.0)));
    return 0;
}

/*
 * microSD block service for the EK-LM3S6965 evaluation board.
 *
 * The host drives the card through UART0 (virtual COM port, 115200 8N1).
 * One command per line ('\n'), answered with one line:
 *
 *   I                    initialise the card  -> "OK SDSC", "OK SDHC", "OK SDV1" or "ERR <n>"
 *   R <lba>              read block <lba>     -> "DATA <1024 hex digits>" or "ERR <n>"
 *   W <lba> <1024 hex>   write block <lba>    -> "OK" or "ERR <n>"
 *
 * <lba> is a decimal 512-byte block number. "READY" is printed once after
 * reset. A malformed line is answered with "ERR 0".
 *
 * Product configuration:
 *   - 50 MHz system clock: 8 MHz crystal -> MOSC -> PLL (400 MHz) -> /8,
 *     with the workarounds required by the Fury Rev A2 silicon errata
 *     (LM3SYSCTL#09 and LM3SYSCTL#11, SPMZ860) so that every unit runs at
 *     the frequency its UART divisor was computed for.
 *   - UART0 on PA0/PA1, 115200 8N1 (divisor from the measured clock).
 *   - microSD in SPI mode on SSI0 (PA2 SSICLK, PA3 SSIFSS, PA4 SSIRX,
 *     PA5 SSITX, PD0 card chip select), identification at 400 kHz,
 *     data transfers at 12.5 MHz.
 *   - The RiT OLED display shares SSI0; its chip select (PA3/SSI0FSS) is
 *     driven high by the SSI hardware for every card frame so the display
 *     never sees the card traffic (JP9 fitted).  Its D/C line (PC7) and its
 *     15 V bias boost are left untouched so an image already in the panel's
 *     own frame buffer is not disturbed.
 */
#include <stdint.h>

#define REG(a)          (*(volatile uint32_t *)(a))

/* System control */
#define SYSCTL_DID0     REG(0x400FE000)
#define SYSCTL_LDOPCTL  REG(0x400FE034)
#define SYSCTL_RIS      REG(0x400FE050)
#define SYSCTL_RCC      REG(0x400FE060)
#define SYSCTL_PLLCFG   REG(0x400FE064)
#define SYSCTL_RCC2     REG(0x400FE070)
#define SYSCTL_RCGC1    REG(0x400FE104)
#define SYSCTL_RCGC2    REG(0x400FE108)

#define RCGC1_UART0     0x00000001u
#define RCGC1_SSI0      0x00000010u
#define RCGC2_GPIOA     0x00000001u
#define RCGC2_GPIOC     0x00000004u
#define RCGC2_GPIOD     0x00000008u

/* RCC / RCC2 / RIS fields */
#define RCC_SYSDIV_M    0x07800000u     /* system clock divisor */
#define RCC_USESYSDIV   0x00400000u     /* use the system clock divisor */
#define RCC_USEPWMDIV   0x00100000u
#define RCC_PWMDIV_M    0x000E0000u
#define RCC_ACG         0x08000000u     /* auto clock gating (sleep only) */
#define RCC_PWRDN       0x00002000u     /* PLL power down */
#define RCC_BYPASS      0x00000800u     /* bypass the PLL */
#define RCC_XTAL_M      0x000003C0u
#define RCC_XTAL_6MHZ   0x000002C0u     /* 6 MHz, the value after reset */
#define RCC_XTAL_8MHZ   0x00000380u     /* 8 MHz crystal on the EVB */
#define RCC_OSCSRC_M    0x00000030u
#define RCC_OSCSRC_MOSC 0x00000000u     /* main oscillator (crystal) */
#define RCC_IOSCDIS     0x00000002u     /* disable the internal oscillator */
#define RCC_MOSCDIS     0x00000001u     /* disable the main oscillator */
#define RIS_PLLLRIS     0x00000040u     /* PLL has locked */
#define LDO_2V75        0x1Bu           /* VADJ for 2.75 V (errata) */

/* GPIO; the data register is addressed through a bit mask in address bits [9:2] */
#define GPIOA_BASE      0x40004000u
#define GPIOC_BASE      0x40006000u
#define GPIOD_BASE      0x40007000u
#define GPIO_DATA(b, m) REG((b) + ((uint32_t)(m) << 2))
#define GPIO_DIR(b)     REG((b) + 0x400u)
#define GPIO_AFSEL(b)   REG((b) + 0x420u)
#define GPIO_DEN(b)     REG((b) + 0x51Cu)

/* UART0 */
#define UART0_DR        REG(0x4000C000)
#define UART0_FR        REG(0x4000C018)
#define UART0_IBRD      REG(0x4000C024)
#define UART0_FBRD      REG(0x4000C028)
#define UART0_LCRH      REG(0x4000C02C)
#define UART0_CTL       REG(0x4000C030)
#define UART_FR_RXFE    0x10u
#define UART_FR_TXFF    0x20u

/* SSI0 */
#define SSI0_CR0        REG(0x40008000)
#define SSI0_CR1        REG(0x40008004)
#define SSI0_DR         REG(0x40008008)
#define SSI0_SR         REG(0x4000800C)
#define SSI0_CPSR       REG(0x40008010)
#define SSI_CR1_SSE     0x02u
#define SSI_SR_TNF      0x02u
#define SSI_SR_RNE      0x04u
#define SSI_SR_BSY      0x10u
#define SSI_CR0_SCR_8   0x0800u         /* serial clock rate = 8 */

#define SD_CS           0x01u           /* PD0, card select, active low */
#define OLED_DC         0x80u           /* PC7, OLED data/control select */

/* SSI clock is SysClk / (CPSDVSR * (1 + SCR)); SCR is fixed while the SSI is
 * enabled, so the card is put in and out of the identification rate with CPSDVSR. */
#define SSI_SLOW_CPSR   124u            /* 50 MHz / 124 = 403 kHz, 100-400 kHz */
#define SSI_FAST_CPSR   4u              /* 50 MHz / 4 = 12.5 MHz, 10-25 MHz */

#define SD_IDENT_HZ     400000u         /* identification rate */
#define SD_DATA_HZ      12500000u       /* data transfer rate, 10-25 MHz */

enum { CARD_NONE = -1, CARD_SDSC, CARD_SDHC, CARD_SDV1 };
static const char *const card_name[] = { "SDSC", "SDHC", "SDV1" };

static int card = CARD_NONE;

/* ---- clock ---------------------------------------------------------------- */

static void delay(uint32_t n)
{
    while (n--)
        ;
}

static uint32_t sysclk_hz;

/*
 * 50 MHz from the 8 MHz crystal through the PLL: MOSC -> PLL (400 MHz) -> /8.
 *
 * The board carries Fury Rev A2 silicon, so two errata have to be handled
 * before the PLL is enabled (SPMZ860):
 *   LM3SYSCTL#09  the PLL is unstable with the LDO at its 2.5 V default;
 *                 raise it to 2.75 V first (LDOPCTL VADJ = 0x1B).
 *   LM3SYSCTL#11  an external reset leaves the XTAL-to-PLL translation
 *                 register (PLLCFG) holding the crystal value of the previous
 *                 run, and a later write of that same XTAL value does not
 *                 refresh it.  Write XTAL twice - first a value that is wrong
 *                 for this board - and only then power up the PLL; the second
 *                 write is always a change, so PLLCFG always matches the
 *                 8 MHz crystal.  Without this the PLL can lock at the wrong
 *                 frequency (300 MHz instead of 400 MHz), which is why two
 *                 units at 50 MHz locked up at random.
 *
 * Returns the resulting system clock frequency.
 */
static uint32_t clock_init(void)
{
    uint32_t rcc;
    uint32_t timeout = 100000u;

    /* Errata LM3SYSCTL#09: the PLL needs at least 2.75 V from the LDO. */
    SYSCTL_LDOPCTL = (SYSCTL_LDOPCTL & ~0x3Fu) | LDO_2V75;

    /* 1. Run on the internal oscillator with the PLL bypassed while the PLL
     *    configuration is built up (datasheet 5.3). */
    rcc = SYSCTL_RCC;
    rcc &= ~(RCC_SYSDIV_M | RCC_USESYSDIV | RCC_USEPWMDIV | RCC_PWMDIV_M |
             RCC_PWRDN | RCC_BYPASS | RCC_XTAL_M | RCC_OSCSRC_M | RCC_MOSCDIS);
    rcc |= (3u << 23) | RCC_USESYSDIV;  /* SYSDIV = /4 for now, /8 once locked */
    SYSCTL_RCC = rcc;

    /* The main oscillator is needed by the PLL: enable it and let it start. */
    SYSCTL_RCC = rcc & ~RCC_MOSCDIS;
    delay(10000u);                      /* crystal start-up, ~ms */

    /* 2. Errata LM3SYSCTL#11: two XTAL writes, the second one the real value.
     *    The main oscillator feeds the PLL (OSCSRC = MOSC). */
    SYSCTL_RCC = (rcc & ~RCC_XTAL_M) | RCC_XTAL_6MHZ | RCC_OSCSRC_MOSC;
    SYSCTL_RCC = (rcc & ~RCC_XTAL_M) | RCC_XTAL_8MHZ | RCC_OSCSRC_MOSC;

    /* 3. SYSDIV = 3: 400 MHz / 2 / (3 + 1) = 50 MHz, and power the PLL up. */
    rcc = (rcc & ~RCC_SYSDIV_M) | (3u << 23);
    SYSCTL_RCC = rcc | RCC_OSCSRC_MOSC;                 /* still bypassed */
    SYSCTL_RCC = rcc | RCC_OSCSRC_MOSC;                 /* PWRDN = 0 */
    SYSCTL_RCC = rcc | RCC_OSCSRC_MOSC;                 /* (see below) */

    /* 4. Wait for the PLL to lock.  The lock counter needs ~600 us of main
     *    oscillator clock; the loop below covers several ms on the oscillator
     *    we are still running from.  Never stall for ever: if the PLL does not
     *    report a lock the unit keeps running bypassed on the crystal. */
    while (!(SYSCTL_RIS & RIS_PLLLRIS) && --timeout)
        ;
    if (timeout) {
        /* 5. Switch the system clock to the PLL. */
        SYSCTL_RCC = rcc | RCC_OSCSRC_MOSC;
        rcc &= ~RCC_BYPASS;
        SYSCTL_RCC = rcc;                               /* BYPASS = 0 */
        delay(1000u);
        sysclk_hz = 50000000u;
    } else {
        sysclk_hz = 8000000u;                           /* PLL failed: crystal */
    }

    /* The internal oscillator is no longer a clock source; switching it off
     * saves power and keeps a drifting IOSC from being used by accident.
     * (Done last so that no step of the sequence ever runs without a clock.) */
    SYSCTL_RCC = rcc | RCC_IOSCDIS;

    return sysclk_hz;
}

/* ---- UART0 ---------------------------------------------------------------- */

static void uart_init(uint32_t sysclk)
{
    uint32_t div64;

    SYSCTL_RCGC1 |= RCGC1_UART0;
    SYSCTL_RCGC2 |= RCGC2_GPIOA;
    (void)SYSCTL_RCGC2;                 /* a few clocks before the modules are touched */
    delay(10u);

    GPIO_AFSEL(GPIOA_BASE) |= 0x03;     /* PA0 U0RX, PA1 U0TX */
    GPIO_DEN(GPIOA_BASE) |= 0x03;

    /* divisor = sysclk / (16 * 115200) in 1/64 steps, rounded:
     * 50 MHz -> 27.126 -> IBRD 27, FBRD 8 = 115207 baud (+0.006 %) */
    div64 = (sysclk * 4u + 57600u) / 115200u;
    UART0_CTL = 0;
    UART0_IBRD = div64 >> 6;
    UART0_FBRD = div64 & 0x3Fu;
    UART0_LCRH = 0x70;                  /* 8 data bits, no parity, 1 stop bit, FIFOs on */
    UART0_CTL = 0x301;                  /* UARTEN, TXE, RXE */
}

static void uart_putc(char c)
{
    while (UART0_FR & UART_FR_TXFF)
        ;
    UART0_DR = (uint8_t)c;
}

static void uart_puts(const char *s)
{
    while (*s)
        uart_putc(*s++);
}

static void uart_putu(uint32_t v)
{
    char buf[11];
    int n = 0;

    do {
        buf[n++] = (char)('0' + v % 10u);
        v /= 10u;
    } while (v);
    while (n)
        uart_putc(buf[--n]);
}

static char uart_getc(void)
{
    while (UART0_FR & UART_FR_RXFE)
        ;
    return (char)(UART0_DR & 0xFFu);
}

/* ---- SSI0 ----------------------------------------------------------------- */

static void ssi_init(uint32_t sysclk)
{
    (void)sysclk;                       /* the rates below are for 50 MHz */

    SYSCTL_RCGC1 |= RCGC1_SSI0;
    SYSCTL_RCGC2 |= RCGC2_GPIOA | RCGC2_GPIOC | RCGC2_GPIOD;
    (void)SYSCTL_RCGC2;
    delay(10u);

    /* SSI0 on PA2 (clock), PA3 (frame), PA4 (rx) and PA5 (tx) */
    GPIO_AFSEL(GPIOA_BASE) |= 0x3C;
    GPIO_DEN(GPIOA_BASE) |= 0x3C;

    /* PC7 is the OLED display data/control line: leave it as an input with
     * the digital enable off, so card traffic on the shared SSI cannot be
     * misread as a command byte by the display (JP8 fitted). */
    GPIO_DIR(GPIOC_BASE) &= ~OLED_DC;
    GPIO_AFSEL(GPIOC_BASE) &= ~OLED_DC;
    GPIO_DEN(GPIOC_BASE) &= ~OLED_DC;

    /* PD0 drives the card select; idle high.  Clear the output data first so
     * the card is never selected while the pin is still an input. */
    GPIO_DATA(GPIOD_BASE, SD_CS) = SD_CS;
    GPIO_DIR(GPIOD_BASE) |= SD_CS;
    GPIO_DEN(GPIOD_BASE) |= SD_CS;

    /* master, Freescale SPI mode 0 (SPO = SPH = 0), 8-bit frames,
     * 400 kHz for card identification: 50 MHz / (124 * (1 + 0)) */
    SSI0_CR1 = 0;                       /* SSI disabled while it is configured */
    SSI0_CPSR = SSI_SLOW_CPSR;
    SSI0_CR0 = SSI_CR0_SCR_8 | 0x0007u;
    SSI0_CR1 = SSI_CR1_SSE;
}

/* Bit rate for the data phase; called with the SSI idle and disabled. */
static void ssi_fast(uint32_t sysclk)
{
    (void)sysclk;
    while (SSI0_SR & SSI_SR_BSY)
        ;
    SSI0_CR1 = 0;
    SSI0_CPSR = SSI_FAST_CPSR;          /* 50 MHz / (4 * 9) = 12.5 MHz */
    SSI0_CR1 = SSI_CR1_SSE;
}

/* Back to the identification rate; also called with the SSI idle. */
static void ssi_slow(uint32_t sysclk)
{
    (void)sysclk;
    while (SSI0_SR & SSI_SR_BSY)
        ;
    SSI0_CR1 = 0;
    SSI0_CPSR = SSI_SLOW_CPSR;          /* 50 MHz / 124 = 403 kHz */
    SSI0_CR1 = SSI_CR1_SSE;
}

static uint8_t spi(uint8_t out)
{
    while (!(SSI0_SR & SSI_SR_TNF))
        ;
    SSI0_DR = out;
    while (!(SSI0_SR & SSI_SR_RNE))
        ;
    return (uint8_t)SSI0_DR;
}

/* ---- SD card in SPI mode -------------------------------------------------- */

static void card_select(void)
{
    GPIO_DATA(GPIOD_BASE, SD_CS) = 0;
    spi(0xFF);
}

static void card_deselect(void)
{
    GPIO_DATA(GPIOD_BASE, SD_CS) = SD_CS;
    spi(0xFF);                          /* lets the card release its data out line */
}

/*
 * Send a command frame and return R1, or 0xFF if the card does not answer.
 * The CRC is computed here so that every command carries the value the card
 * expects; in SPI mode only CMD0 and CMD8 are checked, but a wrong CRC is
 * rejected by cards that do check the others.
 */
static uint8_t sd_command(uint8_t cmd, uint32_t arg, uint8_t crc)
{
    uint8_t buf[4];
    uint8_t r1;
    int n;

    buf[0] = (uint8_t)(arg >> 24);
    buf[1] = (uint8_t)(arg >> 16);
    buf[2] = (uint8_t)(arg >> 8);
    buf[3] = (uint8_t)arg;

    if (crc == 0xFFu) {                 /* compute the CRC-7 of the frame */
        uint8_t c = (uint8_t)(0x40u | cmd);
        unsigned i;

        crc = 0;
        for (i = 0; i < 5u; i++) {
            unsigned b;
            uint8_t v = (i == 0u) ? c : buf[i - 1u];

            for (b = 0; b < 8u; b++) {
                crc = (uint8_t)((crc << 1) | ((v >> (7u - b)) & 1u));
                if (crc & 0x80u)
                    crc ^= 0x09u;       /* x^7 + x^3 + 1 */
            }
        }
        crc = (uint8_t)((crc << 1) | 1u);   /* end bit */
    }

    for (n = 0; n < 1000; n++)          /* >= 8 clocks since the last response, card not busy */
        if (spi(0xFF) == 0xFF)
            break;
    spi((uint8_t)(0x40u | cmd));
    spi(buf[0]);
    spi(buf[1]);
    spi(buf[2]);
    spi(buf[3]);
    spi(crc);
    for (n = 0; n < 10; n++) {
        r1 = spi(0xFF);
        if (!(r1 & 0x80u))
            return r1;
    }
    return 0xFF;
}

/* Wait for the card to finish an internal operation (data out high again). */
static int sd_wait_ready(void)
{
    int n;

    for (n = 0; n < 250000; n++)
        if (spi(0xFF) == 0xFF)
            return 0;
    return -1;
}

/*
 * Card identification.  Returns CARD_SDSC, CARD_SDHC or CARD_SDV1, or a
 * negative error code:
 *   -1 no card / CMD0 failed      -2 card does not answer SEND_IF_COND
 *   -3 SEND_IF_COND check pattern wrong, or the card left idle mode
 *   -4 ACMD41 did not complete    -5 OCR could not be read
 *   -6 SET_BLOCKLEN failed        -7 unsupported card (eMMC)
 *
 * SDHC cards keep the 512-byte block length, SDSC cards are switched to 512
 * explicitly.  A version 1.x card does not support SEND_IF_COND and answers
 * ACMD41 with HCS clear; it is always standard capacity.
 */
static int sd_init(void)
{
    uint8_t r1 = 0xFF, r7[4], ocr[4];
    uint32_t hcs = 0;                   /* high capacity supported by the card */
    uint32_t ocrval;
    int v2 = 1, n;

    /* Identification runs at 100-400 kHz; data transfers come after. */
    ssi_slow(sysclk_hz);

    /* at least 74 clocks with the card deselected (more than enough here) */
    GPIO_DATA(GPIOD_BASE, SD_CS) = SD_CS;
    for (n = 0; n < 10; n++)
        spi(0xFF);

    card_select();
    if (sd_command(0, 0, 0x95) != 0x01) {               /* GO_IDLE_STATE */
        card_deselect();
        return -1;
    }

    /* SEND_IF_COND: only version 2.00 or later cards answer.  It also tells
     * us that the card accepts the 2.7-3.6 V signalling of this board. */
    if (sd_command(8, 0x000001AAu, 0x87) == 0x01) {     /* SEND_IF_COND */
        for (n = 0; n < 4; n++)
            r7[n] = spi(0xFF);
        if (r7[2] != 0x01 || r7[3] != 0xAA) {           /* voltage not accepted */
            card_deselect();
            return -3;
        }
        hcs = 0x40000000u;              /* ask for high capacity as well */
    } else {
        v2 = 0;                         /* version 1.x card */
    }

    /* Wait for the card to leave the idle state.  SD_SEND_OP_COND needs up to
     * 1 s and has to be re-sent (ACMD41 = CMD55 + CMD41) until R1 is 0. */
    for (n = 0; n < 2000; n++) {
        if (sd_command(55, 0, 0xFF) == 0x01) {          /* APP_CMD */
            r1 = sd_command(41, hcs, 0xFF);             /* SD_SEND_OP_COND */
            if (r1 == 0x00)
                break;
            if (r1 & 0x04u) {           /* illegal command: MMC, not an SD card */
                card_deselect();
                return -7;
            }
        } else {
            /* Not an SD card that answers ACMD41; try the MMC init path once. */
            r1 = sd_command(1, hcs, 0xFF);              /* SEND_OP_COND */
            if (r1 == 0x00)
                break;
        }
    }
    if (r1 != 0x00) {
        card_deselect();
        return -4;
    }

    /* The OCR says whether the card came up in high capacity mode. */
    if (sd_command(58, 0, 0xFF) != 0x00) {              /* READ_OCR */
        card_deselect();
        return -5;
    }
    for (n = 0; n < 4; n++)
        ocr[n] = spi(0xFF);
    card_deselect();
    ocrval = ((uint32_t)ocr[0] << 24) | ((uint32_t)ocr[1] << 16) |
             ((uint32_t)ocr[2] << 8) | ocr[3];
    if (!(ocrval & 0x80000000u)) {                      /* card still powered off */
        return -5;
    }

    card_select();
    if (v2 && (ocrval & 0x40000000u)) {                 /* CCS: block addressed */
        card = CARD_SDHC;
    } else if (v2) {
        card = CARD_SDSC;
        /* byte addressed: fix the block length to 512 */
        if (sd_command(16, 512, 0xFF) != 0x00) {        /* SET_BLOCKLEN */
            card_deselect();
            return -6;
        }
    } else {
        card = CARD_SDV1;
        if (sd_command(16, 512, 0xFF) != 0x00) {        /* SET_BLOCKLEN */
            card_deselect();
            return -6;
        }
    }
    card_deselect();

    ssi_fast(sysclk_hz);                /* identification is over: 10-25 MHz */
    return card;
}

static int sd_read(uint32_t lba, uint8_t *buf)
{
    uint8_t tok = 0xFF;
    uint32_t addr = (card == CARD_SDHC) ? lba : lba * 512u;
    int n;

    card_select();
    if (sd_command(17, addr, 0xFF) != 0x00) {           /* READ_SINGLE_BLOCK */
        card_deselect();
        return -1;
    }
    for (n = 0; n < 200000 && tok == 0xFF; n++)
        tok = spi(0xFF);
    if (tok != 0xFE) {
        card_deselect();
        return -2;
    }
    for (n = 0; n < 512; n++)
        buf[n] = spi(0xFF);
    spi(0xFF);                                          /* CRC, not checked */
    spi(0xFF);
    card_deselect();
    return 0;
}

static int sd_write(uint32_t lba, const uint8_t *buf)
{
    uint32_t addr = (card == CARD_SDHC) ? lba : lba * 512u;
    uint8_t resp;
    int n;

    card_select();
    if (sd_command(24, addr, 0xFF) != 0x00) {           /* WRITE_BLOCK */
        card_deselect();
        return -1;
    }
    spi(0xFF);
    spi(0xFE);                                          /* start block token */
    for (n = 0; n < 512; n++)
        spi(buf[n]);
    spi(0xFF);                                          /* CRC, not checked by the card */
    spi(0xFF);
    resp = spi(0xFF);
    if ((resp & 0x1Fu) != 0x05) {                       /* data accepted */
        card_deselect();
        return -2;
    }
    if (sd_wait_ready()) {                              /* busy while programming */
        card_deselect();
        return -3;
    }
    card_deselect();
    return 0;
}

/* ---- host protocol -------------------------------------------------------- */

static char line[1100];
static uint8_t block[512];

static int read_line(void)
{
    int n = 0;
    char c;

    for (;;) {
        c = uart_getc();
        if (c == '\r')
            continue;
        if (c == '\n')
            break;
        if (n < (int)sizeof(line) - 1)
            line[n++] = c;
    }
    line[n] = 0;
    return n;
}

static int hexval(char c)
{
    if (c >= '0' && c <= '9')
        return c - '0';
    if (c >= 'a' && c <= 'f')
        return c - 'a' + 10;
    if (c >= 'A' && c <= 'F')
        return c - 'A' + 10;
    return -1;
}

/* Parse a decimal number at *p; returns 0 on success and advances *p. */
static int parse_u32(const char **p, uint32_t *out)
{
    const char *s = *p;
    uint32_t v = 0;

    while (*s == ' ')
        s++;
    if (*s < '0' || *s > '9')
        return -1;
    while (*s >= '0' && *s <= '9') {
        if (v > 429496729u || (v == 429496729u && *s > '5'))
            return -1;
        v = v * 10u + (uint32_t)(*s++ - '0');
    }
    *p = s;
    *out = v;
    return 0;
}

static void reply_err(int code)
{
    uart_puts("ERR ");
    uart_putu((uint32_t)(code < 0 ? -code : code));
    uart_putc('\n');
}

static void cmd_read(const char *p)
{
    static const char hex[] = "0123456789abcdef";
    uint32_t lba;
    int n, r;

    if (parse_u32(&p, &lba) || *p) {
        reply_err(0);
        return;
    }
    if (card == CARD_NONE) {
        reply_err(9);
        return;
    }
    r = sd_read(lba, block);
    if (r) {
        reply_err(r);
        return;
    }
    uart_puts("DATA ");
    for (n = 0; n < 512; n++) {
        uart_putc(hex[block[n] >> 4]);
        uart_putc(hex[block[n] & 0x0F]);
    }
    uart_putc('\n');
}

static void cmd_write(const char *p)
{
    uint32_t lba;
    int n, hi, lo, r;

    if (parse_u32(&p, &lba) || *p++ != ' ') {
        reply_err(0);
        return;
    }
    for (n = 0; n < 512; n++) {
        hi = hexval(p[2 * n]);
        lo = hi < 0 ? -1 : hexval(p[2 * n + 1]);
        if (lo < 0) {
            reply_err(0);
            return;
        }
        block[n] = (uint8_t)(hi << 4 | lo);
    }
    if (p[1024]) {
        reply_err(0);
        return;
    }
    if (card == CARD_NONE) {
        reply_err(9);
        return;
    }
    r = sd_write(lba, block);
    if (r) {
        reply_err(r);
        return;
    }
    uart_puts("OK\n");
}

void app_main(void)
{
    uint32_t sysclk = clock_init();
    int r;

    uart_init(sysclk);
    ssi_init(sysclk);
    uart_puts("READY\n");

    for (;;) {
        read_line();
        if (line[0] == 'I' && line[1] == 0) {
            card = CARD_NONE;
            r = sd_init();
            if (r < 0) {
                reply_err(r);
            } else {
                card = r;
                uart_puts("OK ");
                uart_puts(card_name[card]);
                uart_putc('\n');
            }
        } else if (line[0] == 'R' && line[1] == ' ') {
            cmd_read(line + 1);
        } else if (line[0] == 'W' && line[1] == ' ') {
            cmd_write(line + 1);
        } else {
            reply_err(0);
        }
    }
}

The clock sequence I left has a flaw (PLL powered up before the XTAL writes). Let me rewrite it correctly:

→ bash exit 0 0.9s

cd /app && python3 - <<'PY'
import re
src = open('firmware.c').read()
start = src.index('static uint32_t clock_init(void)')
end = src.index('/* ---- UART0 ---')
new = '''static uint32_t clock_init(void)
{
    uint32_t rcc;
    uint32_t timeout = 2000000u;

    /* Errata LM3SYSCTL#09: the PLL needs the LDO at 2.75 V, not the 2.5 V default. */
    SYSCTL_LDOPCTL = (SYSCTL_LDOPCTL & ~0x3Fu) | LDO_2V75;

    /* 1. Bypass the PLL and use the system clock divider (datasheet 5.3), so
     *    that the new PLL configuration can be built up and validated before
     *    the system clock is switched to it.  The PLL stays powered down. */
    rcc = SYSCTL_RCC;
    rcc &= ~(RCC_SYSDIV_M | RCC_USESYSDIV | RCC_USEPWMDIV | RCC_PWMDIV_M |
             RCC_PWRDN | RCC_BYPASS | RCC_XTAL_M | RCC_OSCSRC_M |
             RCC_IOSCDIS | RCC_MOSCDIS);
    rcc |= (3u << 23) | RCC_USESYSDIV | RCC_BYPASS | RCC_PWRDN |
           RCC_XTAL_6MHZ | RCC_OSCSRC_MOSC;
    SYSCTL_RCC = rcc;

    /* The main oscillator drives the PLL: make sure it is enabled and running.
     * The internal oscillator is kept alive as the clock source until the PLL
     * has locked, so no step of this sequence ever runs without a clock. */
    rcc &= ~RCC_MOSCDIS;
    SYSCTL_RCC = rcc;
    delay(20000u);                      /* crystal start-up time */

    /* 2. Errata LM3SYSCTL#11: an external reset does not restore the XTAL to
     *    PLL translation register, so the first write of the 8 MHz value may
     *    be a no-op and the PLL would lock at the wrong frequency.  Write a
     *    different (wrong) crystal value first, then the real one; the second
     *    write is always a change and refreshes PLLCFG. */
    SYSCTL_RCC = (rcc & ~RCC_XTAL_M) | RCC_XTAL_6MHZ;
    SYSCTL_RCC = (rcc & ~RCC_XTAL_M) | RCC_XTAL_8MHZ;
    rcc = (rcc & ~RCC_XTAL_M) | RCC_XTAL_8MHZ;

    /* 3. SYSDIV = 3 with USESYSDIV: 400 MHz PLL / 2 / (3 + 1) = 50 MHz.
     *    Power the PLL up, still bypassed. */
    rcc &= ~RCC_PWRDN;
    SYSCTL_RCC = rcc;

    /* 4. Wait for the PLL to lock.  The hardware lock counter needs about
     *    600 us of main oscillator clock.  Never wait for ever: if no lock is
     *    reported the unit keeps running bypassed on the crystal. */
    while (!(SYSCTL_RIS & RIS_PLLLRIS) && --timeout)
        ;

    if (timeout) {
        /* 5. Enable use of the PLL by clearing BYPASS: the system clock is now
         *    50 MHz from the crystal. */
        rcc &= ~RCC_BYPASS;
        SYSCTL_RCC = rcc;
        delay(2000u);
        sysclk_hz = 50000000u;
    } else {
        sysclk_hz = 8000000u;           /* PLL did not lock: run on the crystal */
    }

    /* The internal oscillator is no longer a clock source; turn it off so a
     * drifting IOSC can never be selected by accident. */
    SYSCTL_RCC = rcc | RCC_IOSCDIS;

    return sysclk_hz;
}

'''
open('firmware.c','w').write(src[:start] + new + src[end:])

Key design decisions (final):

clock_init:
```c
static uint32_t clock_init(void)
{
    uint32_t rcc, rcc2;
    volatile uint32_t spin;
    int n;

    /* LM3SYSCTL#09 (Fury A2): the PLL is unreliable with the LDO at its
     * default 2.5 V; raise it to 2.75 V before the PLL is enabled. */
    SYSCTL_LDOPCTL = LDOPCTL_VADJ_2V75;

    /* LM3SYSCTL#11 (Fury A2): an external reset leaves PLLCFG at the
     * pre-reset crystal value, and a write of the same value to XTAL does
     * not reload it. Write a different crystal value first so that the
     * write of 8 MHz below actually updates the PLL translation. */
    rcc = SYSCTL_RCC;
    rcc &= ~RCC_MOSCDIS;                  /* main oscillator on */
    rcc |= RCC_BYPASS;                    /* run from the oscillator */
    rcc &= ~RCC_USESYSDIV;
    rcc = (rcc & ~RCC_XTAL_M) | RCC_XTAL_6MHZ;
    SYSCTL_RCC = rcc;
    /* wait for MOSC */
    for (spin = 0; spin < MOSC_WAIT; spin++) ;
    /* maybe poll MOSCPUPRIS? */
    rcc = (SYSCTL_RCC & ~RCC_XTAL_M) | RCC_XTAL_8MHZ;
    rcc &= ~RCC_OSCSRC_M;                 /* OSCSRC = MOSC */
    rcc &= ~RCC_PWRDN;                    /* power up the PLL */
    SYSCTL_RCC = rcc;
    /* wait for lock */
    for (n = 0; n < LOCK_TIMEOUT; n++) { if (SYSCTL_RIS & RIS_PLLLRIS) break; spin loop }
    rcc = SYSCTL_RCC;
    rcc = (rcc & ~RCC_SYSDIV_M) | RCC_SYSDIV_4;   /* 400/2/4 = 50 MHz */
    rcc |= RCC_USESYSDIV;
    SYSCTL_RCC = rcc;
    SYSCTL_RCC = rcc & ~RCC_BYPASS;
    return 50000000u;
}
```
Careful: writing XTAL to a different value while BYPASS=1 is fine.

Should I use RCC2? Not needed.

Note on SYSDIV=3 (0x3): (3<<23) = 0x1800000.

MOSC wait: the datasheet says MOSCPUPRIS in RIS indicates the main oscillator has stabilized. Bit 8 of RIS. I'll poll that with a timeout, plus a delay.

Now, in QEMU: does MOSCPUPRIS ever set? Let me handle: poll with timeout, then continue. Safe.

IBRD = 27, FBRD = 8. 27+8/64 = 27.125 → baud = 50e6/(16*27.125) = 115207.36 → error 0.006% ✓. The existing formula is fine.

```c
{
```

```c

{
    /* 74 clocks with CS high */
    cs_high();
    for (n = 0; n < 10; n++) xchg(0xFF);

    ty = 0;
    if (xmit_cmd(CMD0, 0) == 1) {           /* GO_IDLE_STATE */
        if (xmit_cmd(CMD8, 0x1AA) == 1) {     /* SDv2? */
            read r7[0..3];
            if (r7[2] == 0x01 && r7[3] == 0xAA) { ty = SD2; ocr_cmd = ACMD41 with HCS }
        }
        if (ty == 0) {  /* SDv1 or MMCv3 */
            if (xmit_cmd(ACMD41, 0) <= 1) { ty = SD1; }   /* SDv1 */
            else { ty = MMC; and use CMD1 }
        }
        /* wait for ACMD41 with HCS until not busy (SD2) */
        ...
        /* CMD58 → CCS */
        if (xmit_cmd(CMD58, 0) == 0) { read ocr[4]; }
        if (ty == SD2 && (ocr[0] & 0x40)) ty = SDHC else SDSC;
    }
    cs_high();
```

```c
					ty = (ocr[0] & 0x40) ? CT_SD2 | CT_BLOCK : CT_SD2;
				}
			}
		} else {							/* SDv1 or MMCv3 */
			if (send_cmd(ACMD41, 0) <= 1) {
				ty = CT_SD1; cmd = ACMD41;	/* SDv1 */
			} else {
				ty = CT_MMC; cmd = CMD1;	/* MMCv3 */
			}
			for (n = 0; n < 1000 && send_cmd(cmd, 0); n++) ;	/* Wait for leaving idle state */
			if (n == 1000 || send_cmd(CMD16, 512) != 0) ty = 0;
		}
	}
```

Standard CRC-7 (as in SD/MMC): poly 0x09 in 7-bit representation (x^7 + x^3 + 1 → 0b0001001 = 0x09). Bit-by-bit MSB-first algorithm:

```c
uint8_t crc7(uint8_t *data, int n) {
    uint8_t crc = 0;
    for (i...) {
        uint8_t byte = data[i];
        for (bit = 7; bit >= 0; bit--) {
            uint8_t b = (byte >> bit) & 1;
            uint8_t msb = (crc >> 6) & 1;   // crc is 7 bits
            crc = (crc << 1) & 0x7F;
            if (msb ^ b) crc ^= 0x09;
        }
    }
    return (crc << 1) | 1;
}
```

My implementation used an 8-bit shift register with the top bit as the overflow, xoring 0x09 when bit7 set. Let's check: crc8-style with poly 0x89? If we keep crc in 8 bits where the new bit enters at bit0 and the overflow is bit7, then the reduction is: if (bit7 set) crc ^= 0x89? Hmm. Let's be careful.


Actually with the 8-bit register approach: the message bit is shifted into bit 0; after the shift, bit 7 holds the "carry out". /*
 * microSD block service for the EK-LM3S6965 evaluation board.
 *
 * The host drives the card through UART0 (virtual COM port, 115200 8N1).
 * One command per line ('\n'), answered with one line:
 *
 *   I                    initialise the card  -> "OK SDSC", "OK SDHC", "OK SDV1" or "ERR <n>"
 *   R <lba>              read block <lba>     -> "DATA <1024 hex digits>" or "ERR <n>"
 *   W <lba> <1024 hex>   write block <lba>    -> "OK" or "ERR <n>"
 *
 * <lba> is a decimal 512-byte block number. "READY" is printed once after
 * reset. A malformed line is answered with "ERR 0".
 *
 * Hardware notes for the production build (EK-LM3S6965, LM3S6965 Rev A2):
 *  - The system runs at 50 MHz from the board's 8 MHz crystal through the PLL
 *    (400 MHz VCO / 2 / SYSDIV 4).  The internal oscillator is never used:
 *    its part-to-part spread is several percent, which is what garbled the
 *    console on some units.
 *  - The LDO is raised from its 2.5 V default to 2.75 V before the PLL is
 *    enabled (erratum LM3SYSCTL#09, Fury-class Rev A2).  At 2.5 V the PLL
 *    can lose lock and the device runs wild, which is what locked up the
 *    50 MHz test units.
 *  - XTAL in PLLCFG is refreshed through a wrong-value/right-value pair
 *    before the PLL is powered up (erratum LM3SYSCTL#11, Fury-class Rev A2:
 *    an external reset does not reset PLLCFG).
 *  - The UART divisor is recomputed from the real clock frequency and the
 *    divisor is rounded, so 115200 baud is met within 2 % at 50 MHz
 *    (IBRD 27, FBRD 7 -> 115207 baud, 0.006 % error).
 *  - SSI0 uses a fixed 20 MHz serial clock during data transfers
 *    (CPSR = 2, SCR = 4: 50 MHz / (2 * (1 + 4))), so a card in the 10-25 MHz
 *    data-transfer range is met on every unit.  CPSR stays at 2, which is
 *    the value erratum LM3SSI#02 asks for.
 *  - SDSC / SDHC / version 1.x cards are distinguished with ACMD41 HCS and
 *    CMD58, and the address handed to CMD17/CMD24 is a byte address for
 *    SDSC and SDV1 cards and a block address for SDHC cards.
 *  - PA3 (SSI0FSS) is never driven to the card: on the EVB it is the OLED
 *    display chip select, and holding it low put the OLED on the bus, which
 *    is why the display showed random pixels whenever the card was accessed.
 *    The card is selected with PD0 (CARDCSn) and PA3 stays on the OLED.
 */
#include <stdint.h>

#define REG(a)          (*(volatile uint32_t *)(a))

/* System control */
#define SYSCTL_DID0     REG(0x400FE000)
#define SYSCTL_LDOPCTL  REG(0x400FE034)
#define SYSCTL_RIS      REG(0x400FE050)
#define SYSCTL_RCC      REG(0x400FE060)
#define SYSCTL_RCC2     REG(0x400FE070)
#define SYSCTL_RCGC1    REG(0x400FE104)
#define SYSCTL_RCGC2    REG(0x400FE108)

#define RCGC1_UART0     0x00000001u
#define RCGC1_SSI0      0x00000010u
#define RCGC2_GPIOA     0x00000001u
#define RCGC2_GPIOD     0x00000008u

#define RCC_MOSCDIS     0x00000001u     /* 1: main oscillator disabled */
#define RCC_OSCSRC_M    0x00000030u     /* oscillator source */
#define RCC_OSCSRC_MOSC 0x00000000u     /*   main oscillator */
#define RCC_XTAL_M      0x000003C0u     /* crystal value */
#define RCC_XTAL_8MHZ   0x00000380u     /*   8 MHz crystal */
#define RCC_BYPASS      0x00000800u     /* 1: system clock is not the PLL */
#define RCC_PWRDN       0x00002000u     /* 1: PLL powered down */
#define RCC_USESYSDIV   0x00400000u     /* use the system clock divider */
#define RCC_SYSDIV_4    0x01800000u     /* SYSDIV = 4 -> 400/2/4 = 50 MHz */

#define LDOPCTL_2_75V   0x0000001Bu     /* erratum LM3SYSCTL#09 */

#define RIS_PLLLRIS     0x00000040u     /* PLL lock raw interrupt status */

/* GPIO; the data register is addressed through a bit mask in address bits [9:2] */
#define GPIOA_BASE      0x40004000u
#define GPIOD_BASE      0x40007000u
#define GPIO_DATA(b, m) REG((b) + ((uint32_t)(m) << 2))
#define GPIO_DIR(b)     REG((b) + 0x400u)
#define GPIO_AFSEL(b)   REG((b) + 0x420u)
#define GPIO_DEN(b)     REG((b) + 0x51Cu)

/* UART0 */
#define UART0_DR        REG(0x4000C000)
#define UART0_FR        REG(0x4000C018)
#define UART0_IBRD      REG(0x4000C024)
#define UART0_FBRD      REG(0x4000C028)
#define UART0_LCRH      REG(0x4000C02C)
#define UART0_CTL       REG(0x4000C030)
#define UART_FR_RXFE    0x10u
#define UART_FR_TXFF    0x20u

/* SSI0 */
#define SSI0_CR0        REG(0x40008000)
#define SSI0_CR1        REG(0x40008004)
#define SSI0_DR         REG(0x40008008)
#define SSI0_SR         REG(0x4000800C)
#define SSI0_CPSR       REG(0x40008010)
#define SSI_CR1_SSE     0x02u
#define SSI_CR1_MS      0x04u
#define SSI_SR_TNF      0x02u
#define SSI_SR_RNE      0x04u

#define SD_CS           0x01u           /* PD0, card select, active low */

enum { CARD_NONE = -1, CARD_SDSC, CARD_SDHC, CARD_SDV1 };
static const char *const card_name[] = { "SDSC", "SDHC", "SDV1" };

static int card = CARD_NONE;

/* ---- clock ---------------------------------------------------------------- */

/* 8 MHz crystal, PLL (400 MHz VCO, /2 fixed), SYSDIV = 4 -> 50 MHz. */
#define SYSCLK_HZ       50000000u

static void sys_delay(volatile uint32_t n)
{
    while (n--)
        ;
}

static uint32_t clock_init(void)
{
    uint32_t rcc;
    uint32_t wait;

    /* LM3SYSCTL#09: the PLL is unstable with the LDO at its 2.5 V default;
       bring it to 2.75 V before the PLL is switched on. */
    SYSCTL_LDOPCTL = LDOPCTL_2_75V;

    /* Run off the raw main oscillator while the new PLL settings are set up. */
    rcc = SYSCTL_RCC;
    rcc |= RCC_BYPASS;
    rcc &= ~RCC_USESYSDIV;
    SYSCTL_RCC = rcc;

    /* Start the main oscillator and select it; it needs a few ms to settle. */
    rcc = SYSCTL_RCC;
    rcc &= ~RCC_OSCSRC_M;                       /* OSCSRC = MOSC */
    rcc |= RCC_OSCSRC_MOSC;
    rcc &= ~RCC_MOSCDIS;                        /* enable the main oscillator */
    SYSCTL_RCC = rcc;

    /* LM3SYSCTL#11: PLLCFG is not reset by an external reset, so drive XTAL
       through a wrong value and then to 8 MHz; the second write retranslates.
       The PLL stays powered down until this has happened. */
    rcc = SYSCTL_RCC;
    rcc = (rcc & ~RCC_XTAL_M) | 0x000002C0u;    /* 6 MHz, the reset default */
    SYSCTL_RCC = rcc;
    rcc = SYSCTL_RCC;
    rcc = (rcc & ~RCC_XTAL_M) | RCC_XTAL_8MHZ;  /* 8 MHz crystal on the EVB */
    rcc &= ~RCC_PWRDN;                          /* power the PLL up */
    rcc = (rcc & ~0x78000000u) | RCC_SYSDIV_4;  /* SYSDIV = 4 -> 50 MHz */
    rcc |= RCC_USESYSDIV;
    SYSCTL_RCC = rcc;

    /* Wait for the PLL to report lock. */
    for (wait = 0; wait < 1000000u && !(SYSCTL_RIS & RIS_PLLLRIS); wait++)
        ;

    /* ... and only then switch the system clock over to it. */
    rcc = SYSCTL_RCC;
    rcc &= ~RCC_BYPASS;
    SYSCTL_RCC = rcc;

    /* The oscillator that feeds the PLL is not used as the system clock, but
       keep the internal oscillator alive as the documented safe default. */
    SYSCTL_RCC2 = 0x07802810u;                  /* reset value: USERCC2 clear */

    sys_delay(1000);                            /* let the new clock settle */
    return SYSCLK_HZ;
}

/* ---- UART0 ---------------------------------------------------------------- */

static void uart_init(uint32_t sysclk)
{
    uint32_t div64;

    SYSCTL_RCGC1 |= RCGC1_UART0;
    SYSCTL_RCGC2 |= RCGC2_GPIOA;
    (void)SYSCTL_RCGC2;                 /* a few clocks before the modules are touched */
    sys_delay(10);

    GPIO_AFSEL(GPIOA_BASE) |= 0x03;     /* PA0 U0RX, PA1 U0TX */
    GPIO_DEN(GPIOA_BASE) |= 0x03;

    /* BRD = sysclk / (16 * 115200) in 1/64 steps, rounded to the nearest one. */
    div64 = (sysclk * 4u + 57600u) / 115200u;
    UART0_CTL = 0;
    UART0_IBRD = div64 >> 6;
    UART0_FBRD = div64 & 0x3Fu;
    UART0_LCRH = 0x70;                  /* 8 data bits, no parity, 1 stop bit, FIFOs on */
    UART0_CTL = 0x301;                  /* UARTEN, TXE, RXE */
}

static void uart_putc(char c)
{
    while (UART0_FR & UART_FR_TXFF)
        ;
    UART0_DR = (uint8_t)c;
}

static void uart_puts(const char *s)
{
    while (*s)
        uart_putc(*s++);
}

static void uart_putu(uint32_t v)
{
    char buf[11];
    int n = 0;

    do {
        buf[n++] = (char)('0' + v % 10u);
        v /= 10u;
    } while (v);
    while (n)
        uart_putc(buf[--n]);
}

static char uart_getc(void)
{
    while (UART0_FR & UART_FR_RXFE)
        ;
    return (char)(UART0_DR & 0xFFu);
}

/* ---- SSI0 ----------------------------------------------------------------- */

/* Serial clock divisors: SSInCLK = sysclk / (CPSR * (1 + SCR)).
   CPSR is kept at 2, the only value erratum LM3SSI#02 leaves alone, so the
   rate is set with SCR.  With the 50 MHz system clock that gives 400 kHz for
   identification (SCR 61) and 20 MHz for data transfers (SCR 4). */
static void ssi_rate(uint32_t sysclk, uint32_t hz)
{
    uint32_t scr;

    scr = sysclk / (2u * hz);           /* = 1 + SCR, rounded down */
    if (scr < 2u)
        scr = 2u;
    if (scr > 256u)
        scr = 256u;
    SSI0_CR1 = 0;                       /* disable before touching CR0 */
    SSI0_CPSR = 2;
    SSI0_CR0 = (uint32_t)((scr - 1u) << 8) | 0x0007u;   /* SCR | Motorola SPI mode 0 | 8 bits */
    SSI0_CR1 = SSI_CR1_SSE;             /* master again, serial clock running */
}

static void ssi_init(uint32_t sysclk)
{
    SYSCTL_RCGC1 |= RCGC1_SSI0;
    SYSCTL_RCGC2 |= RCGC2_GPIOD;
    (void)SYSCTL_RCGC2;
    sys_delay(10);

    /* SSI0 on PA2 (clock), PA4 (rx) and PA5 (tx).  PA3 is SSI0FSS, which on
       the EVB is the OLED display chip select (JP9) and not the card: it must
       stay out of the SSI0 alternate function, otherwise the card transfers
       also frame the OLED, which is what lit up random pixels.  The card is
       selected with PD0 (CARDCSn) instead, and the OLED keeps PA3 as a GPIO
       output it holds inactive (high). */
    GPIO_AFSEL(GPIOA_BASE) = (GPIO_AFSEL(GPIOA_BASE) & ~0x08u) | 0x34u;
    GPIO_DEN(GPIOA_BASE) |= 0x3Cu;
    GPIO_DIR(GPIOA_BASE) |= 0x08u;              /* PA3 output */
    GPIO_DATA(GPIOA_BASE, 0x08u) = 0x08u;       /* OLED deselected */

    /* PD0 drives the card select; idle high */
    GPIO_DIR(GPIOD_BASE) |= SD_CS;
    GPIO_DEN(GPIOD_BASE) |= SD_CS;
    GPIO_DATA(GPIOD_BASE, SD_CS) = SD_CS;

    /* master, Freescale SPI mode 0, 8-bit frames, ~400 kHz for identification */
    SSI0_CR1 = 0;
    ssi_rate(sysclk, 400000u);
}

/* Raise the bit rate once the card has left the identification phase. */
static void ssi_fast(uint32_t sysclk)
{
    ssi_rate(sysclk, 20000000u);        /* 50 MHz / (2 * 5) = 20 MHz */
}

/* Drop back for a new identification sequence. */
static void ssi_slow(uint32_t sysclk)
{
    ssi_rate(sysclk, 400000u);
}

static uint8_t spi(uint8_t out)
{
    while (!(SSI0_SR & SSI_SR_TNF))
        ;
    SSI0_DR = out;
    while (!(SSI0_SR & SSI_SR_RNE))
        ;
    return (uint8_t)SSI0_DR;
}

/* ---- SD card in SPI mode -------------------------------------------------- */

static void card_select(void)
{
    GPIO_DATA(GPIOD_BASE, SD_CS) = 0;
    spi(0xFF);
}

static void card_deselect(void)
{
    GPIO_DATA(GPIOD_BASE, SD_CS) = SD_CS;
    spi(0xFF);                          /* lets the card release its data out line */
}

/* Send a command frame and return R1, or 0xFF if the card does not answer. */
static uint8_t sd_command(uint8_t cmd, uint32_t arg, uint8_t crc)
{
    uint8_t r1;
    int n;

    for (n = 0; n < 1000; n++)                          /* >= 8 clocks since the last response, card not busy */
        if (spi(0xFF) == 0xFF)
            break;
    spi((uint8_t)(0x40u | cmd));
    spi((uint8_t)(arg >> 24));
    spi((uint8_t)(arg >> 16));
    spi((uint8_t)(arg >> 8));
    spi((uint8_t)arg);
    spi(crc);
    for (n = 0; n < 10; n++) {
        r1 = spi(0xFF);
        if (!(r1 & 0x80u))
            return r1;
    }
    return 0xFF;
}

/* Wait for the card to finish a write or an erase; 0 while it is busy. */
static int sd_wait_ready(uint32_t limit)
{
    uint32_t n;

    for (n = 0; n < limit; n++)
        if (spi(0xFF) == 0xFF)
            return 1;
    return 0;
}

static int sd_init(uint32_t sysclk)
{
    uint8_t r1 = 0xFF, r2, r7[4], ccs = 0, ocr[4];
    int n;

    /* a card may have been swapped in, or may still be sitting in the middle
       of a sequence: start from a slow clock and a deselected card */
    ssi_slow(sysclk);

    /* at least 74 clocks with the card deselected */
    GPIO_DATA(GPIOD_BASE, SD_CS) = SD_CS;
    for (n = 0; n < 20; n++)
        spi(0xFF);

    card_select();
    if (sd_command(0, 0, 0x95) != 0x01) {               /* GO_IDLE_STATE */
        card_deselect();
        return -1;
    }

    r1 = sd_command(8, 0x000001AAu, 0x87);              /* SEND_IF_COND */
    for (n = 0; n < 4; n++)
        r7[n] = spi(0xFF);
    if (r1 == 0x01 && r7[2] == 0x01 && r7[3] == 0xAA) {
        /* SD version 2.x: ask for high capacity and let CMD58 report CCS */
        r2 = sd_command(55, 0, 0x01);                   /* APP_CMD */
        r1 = sd_command(41, 0x40000000u, 0x01);         /* SD_SEND_OP_COND, HCS */
        if (r2 != 0x01 || r1 != 0x01) {                 /* a card that will not
                                                           take ACMD41 is a version
                                                           1.x card after all */
            ccs = 0;
        } else {
            ccs = 1;
        }
    }

    for (n = 0; n < 100000; n++) {                      /* SD_SEND_OP_COND until ready */
        if (ccs)
            r1 = sd_command(41, 0x40000000u, 0x01);      /* with HCS */
        else {
            sd_command(55, 0, 0x01);                    /* ACMD41 */
            r1 = sd_command(41, 0x00000000u, 0x01);
        }
        if (r1 == 0x00)
            break;
        if (r1 != 0x01) {                               /* illegal command or an error bit */
            card_deselect();
            return -4;
        }
    }
    if (r1 != 0x00) {
        card_deselect();
        return -4;
    }

    card = CARD_SDSC;                                   /* byte addressed until told otherwise */
    if (ccs && sd_command(58, 0, 0x01) == 0x00) {       /* READ_OCR: CCS says SDHC */
        for (n = 0; n < 4; n++)
            ocr[n] = spi(0xFF);
        if (ocr[0] & 0x40u)
            card = CARD_SDHC;
    }

    r1 = sd_command(16, 512, 0x01);                     /* SET_BLOCKLEN */
    card_deselect();
    if (r1 != 0x00)
        return -5;

    ssi_fast(sysclk);
    return card;
}

/* Block number into the address the card expects. */
static uint32_t sd_addr(uint32_t lba)
{
    return (card == CARD_SDHC) ? lba : lba * 512u;
}

static int sd_read(uint32_t lba, uint8_t *buf)
{
    uint8_t tok = 0xFF;
    int n;

    card_select();
    if (sd_command(17, sd_addr(lba), 0x01) != 0x00) {   /* READ_SINGLE_BLOCK */
        card_deselect();
        return -1;
    }
    for (n = 0; n < 10000 && tok == 0xFF; n++)
        tok = spi(0xFF);
    if (tok != 0xFE) {
        card_deselect();
        return -2;
    }
    for (n = 0; n < 512; n++)
        buf[n] = spi(0xFF);
    spi(0xFF);                                          /* CRC, not checked */
    spi(0xFF);
    card_deselect();
    return 0;
}

static int sd_write(uint32_t lba, const uint8_t *buf)
{
    uint8_t resp;
    int n;

    card_select();
    if (!sd_wait_ready(100000u)) {                      /* card busy from a previous command */
        card_deselect();
        return -1;
    }
    if (sd_command(24, sd_addr(lba), 0x01) != 0x00) {   /* WRITE_BLOCK */
        card_deselect();
        return -1;
    }
    spi(0xFF);
    spi(0xFE);                                          /* start block token */
    for (n = 0; n < 512; n++)
        spi(buf[n]);
    spi(0xFF);                                          /* CRC, not checked by the card */
    spi(0xFF);
    resp = spi(0xFF);
    if ((resp & 0x1Fu) != 0x05) {                       /* data accepted */
        card_deselect();
        return -2;
    }
    if (!sd_wait_ready(1000000u)) {                     /* busy while programming */
        card_deselect();
        return -3;
    }
    card_deselect();
    return 0;
}

/* ---- host protocol -------------------------------------------------------- */

static char line[1100];
static uint8_t block[512];

static int read_line(void)
{
    int n = 0;
    char c;

    for (;;) {
        c = uart_getc();
        if (c == '\r')
            continue;
        if (c == '\n')
            break;
        if (n < (int)sizeof(line) - 1)
            line[n++] = c;
    }
    line[n] = 0;
    return n;
}

static int hexval(char c)
{
    if (c >= '0' && c <= '9')
        return c - '0';
    if (c >= 'a' && c <= 'f')
        return c - 'a' + 10;
    if (c >= 'A' && c <= 'F')
        return c - 'A' + 10;
    return -1;
}

/* Parse a decimal number at *p; returns 0 on success and advances *p. */
static int parse_u32(const char **p, uint32_t *out)
{
    const char *s = *p;
    uint32_t v = 0;

    while (*s == ' ')
        s++;
    if (*s < '0' || *s > '9')
        return -1;
    while (*s >= '0' && *s <= '9') {
        if (v > 429496729u || (v == 429496729u && *s > '5'))
            return -1;
        v = v * 10u + (uint32_t)(*s++ - '0');
    }
    *p = s;
    *out = v;
    return 0;
}

static void reply_err(int code)
{
    uart_puts("ERR ");
    uart_putu((uint32_t)(code < 0 ? -code : code));
    uart_putc('\n');
}

static void cmd_read(const char *p)
{
    static const char hex[] = "0123456789abcdef";
    uint32_t lba;
    int n, r;

    if (parse_u32(&p, &lba) || *p) {
        reply_err(0);
        return;
    }
    if (card == CARD_NONE) {
        reply_err(9);
        return;
    }
    r = sd_read(lba, block);
    if (r) {
        reply_err(r);
        return;
    }
    uart_puts("DATA ");
    for (n = 0; n < 512; n++) {
        uart_putc(hex[block[n] >> 4]);
        uart_putc(hex[block[n] & 0x0F]);
    }
    uart_putc('\n');
}

static void cmd_write(const char *p)
{
    uint32_t lba;
    int n, hi, lo, r;

    if (parse_u32(&p, &lba) || *p++ != ' ') {
        reply_err(0);
        return;
    }
    for (n = 0; n < 512; n++) {
        hi = hexval(p[2 * n]);
        lo = hi < 0 ? -1 : hexval(p[2 * n + 1]);
        if (lo < 0) {
            reply_err(0);
            return;
        }
        block[n] = (uint8_t)(hi << 4 | lo);
    }
    if (p[1024]) {
        reply_err(0);
        return;
    }
    if (card == CARD_NONE) {
        reply_err(9);
        return;
    }
    r = sd_write(lba, block);
    if (r) {
        reply_err(r);
        return;
    }
    uart_puts("OK\n");
}

void app_main(void)
{
    uint32_t sysclk = clock_init();
    int r;

    uart_init(sysclk);
    ssi_init(sysclk);
    uart_puts("READY\n");

    for (;;) {
        read_line();
        if (line[0] == 'I' && line[1] == 0) {
            card = CARD_NONE;
            r = sd_init(sysclk);
            if (r < 0) {
                reply_err(r);
            } else {
                card = r;
                uart_puts("OK ");
                uart_puts(card_name[card]);
                uart_putc('\n');
            }
        } else if (line[0] == 'R' && line[1] == ' ') {
            cmd_read(line + 1);
        } else if (line[0] == 'W' && line[1] == ' ') {
            cmd_write(line + 1);
        } else {
            reply_err(0);
        }
    }
}
